docPurpose: A developer guide that classifies which client/src UI files are actively used in production vs. demo/unused/example/reference implementations, so developers avoid editing dead files and understand the real import chain from the app root.
summary: The guide is substantially outdated and describes a much earlier version of the ClientIQ frontend. Its core premise (file usage classification) is still useful, but nearly every concrete fact is wrong: the routing configuration is entirely obsolete (old /household/:id and /household/optionN routes are now commented out, and current /ciq/*, /account/:accountId, /rbr routes are missing), the app shell is described as TopBar imported by App.tsx when the real shell is Header + Navbar, and many components listed as ACTIVE (RiskCompliance, HouseholdRelationships, AccountCard, TotalRelationshipSummary) are actually unused or in dead branches while many current components (Middle, AccountDetailOption2, AccountList, CustomerSearch in header, the navbar/header/RBR shells, MaintenanceItems) are undocumented. The examples directory has 8 files (matches) but the shadcn "50+ / all ACTIVE" claim is wrong (47 files, and the app is predominantly MUI so ui/* is largely unused scaffolding). Counts, the import-chain tree, and the "safe to delete" list are all keyed to the stale structure.

docPurpose: Entity-Relationship Diagram / data model reference for the ClientIQ (Banking Client 360) database: tables, columns, foreign keys, cardinality, constraints, indexes, and migration/growth guidance.
summary: This ERD is badly out of date and materially wrong in several places. It is framed as a dual-engine (PostgreSQL 14+ | SQL Server 2019+) model when SQL Server is the only production engine; PostgreSQL/pg_trgm/GIN/trigger content is a non-production abstraction that should be demoted. It documents a debit_card_id foreign key and a debit_card->financial_transaction relationship that do not exist in shared/schema.ts, and an account.sic_code FK that also does not exist. It omits entire current domains (Notes module, RBAC/roles/permissions, User Management history/approval tables, audit_event, region, account_sic_code) — the schema has 40 pgTable definitions vs the ~19 depicted. It should be regenerated from shared/schema.ts as a Mermaid ER diagram. Constraint, trigger, index-strategy, and migration-graph sections are stale or reference non-existent objects.

findings.location: Header (top of doc) — "Database Engines: PostgreSQL 14+ | SQL Server 2019+"
findings.docSays: Database Engines: PostgreSQL 14+ | SQL Server 2019+ — presenting the schema as a co-equal dual-engine model.
findings.actualState: SQL Server is the only production engine. server/dbConnection.ts is 'MS SQL Server only (on-prem deployment)'; getPgDatabase() throws 'getPgDatabase() is not available — this deployment uses MS SQL only' (server/dbConnection.ts:74-79). The pgTable schema (shared/schema.ts) and drizzle.config.ts (dialect=postgresql) are a residual type/tooling abstraction, not a runtime engine.
findings.recommendedChange: Change to 'Database Engine: SQL Server 2019+ (production)'. Note that shared/schema.ts is authored in Drizzle pg-core (pgTable) for type generation only, and that Postgres is not a runtime target. Remove the dual-engine framing throughout.

findings.location: FINANCIAL TRANSACTION FLOW box; DEBIT CARD ARCHITECTURE box; One-to-Many table (debit_card->financial_transaction); Business Rule Enforcement Map (FK debit_card_id ... ON DELETE SET NULL); Index Strategy (debit_card_id, posting_date DESC)
findings.docSays: financial_transaction has 'FK debit_card_id (optional) → debit_card', a 1:M debit_card→financial_transaction relationship, an FK 'debit_card_id → debit_card(card_id) ON DELETE SET NULL', and an index on (debit_card_id, posting_date DESC).
findings.actualState: The financial_transaction table (shared/schema.ts:380-425) has NO debit_card_id column, no FK to debit_card, and no such index. Its FKs are only account_id, category_id, and counterparty_account_id. (A stale code comment at shared/schema.ts:448 also claims this linkage, but the table definition contradicts it.)
findings.recommendedChange: Remove all debit_card_id references from the financial_transaction depiction, the debit_card↔transaction 1:M relationship, the ON DELETE SET NULL FK, and the (debit_card_id, posting_date) index. If a card↔transaction link is desired, flag as a known gap; it does not exist in the schema today.

findings.location: CORE BANKING ENTITIES — ACCOUNT box ('FK sic_code'); Business Rule Enforcement Map — 'ACCOUNT TABLE FK: sic_code → sic_code table'
findings.docSays: The account table has 'FK sic_code' referencing the sic_code table for industry classification validation.
findings.actualState: The account table (shared/schema.ts:188-219) has only one FK: branch_id → branch. There is no sic_code column/FK on account. Account↔SIC classification is modeled via the separate account_sic_code junction table (shared/schema.ts:348-363), which the ERD does not depict.
findings.recommendedChange: Remove 'FK sic_code' from the account box and the constraint map. Add the account_sic_code junction table (account_id + sic_code, unique unq_account_sic) to represent account↔SIC as M:N.

findings.location: Entire ERD body — Complete Entity Relationship Overview and all module diagrams
findings.docSays: Depicts roughly 19 tables (customer, account, household, branch, employee, debit_card, online_banking_*, contact_history, sic_code, transaction_category, entity_address/contact, the junctions).
findings.actualState: shared/schema.ts defines 40 pgTable objects. Entirely absent from the ERD: the whole Notes module (note, note_category, note_version, note_audit_log — schema.ts:559-647), the whole RBAC domain (privilege_level, role, permission, role_permission, employee_role, saml_role_mapping, role_audit_log, permission_denial_log — schema.ts:654-778), the User Management tables (employee_status_history, employee_role_history, role_change_request — schema.ts:785-848), audit_event (schema.ts:854-887), region (schema.ts:24-30), and account_sic_code (schema.ts:348-363).
findings.recommendedChange: Regenerate the ERD from shared/schema.ts as a Mermaid erDiagram covering all 40 tables, grouped by domain (Core Banking, Notes, RBAC/Roles, User Management, Audit). This is the single biggest gap: entire production domains are undocumented.

findings.location: Index Strategy Map — 'CUSTOMER SEARCH: PostgreSQL: GIN index on full_name using pg_trgm ... full_name % term'; Customer Search Flow — 'PostgreSQL: pg_trgm SIMILARITY() search'
findings.docSays: Customer search uses a PostgreSQL GIN index on full_name via pg_trgm with the '%' similarity operator as a first-class strategy.
findings.actualState: pg_trgm/similarity() lives only in server/adapters/search/PostgresSearchProvider.ts (:17-18,86-89), which is the non-production path selected only when DB_VENDOR defaults to/equals postgres. Production uses server/adapters/search/SqlServerSearchProvider.ts: STRING_SIMILARITY() on SQL Server 2022+, falling back to SOUNDEX/DIFFERENCE on 2019 (SqlServerSearchProvider.ts:114-129,157,194). No GIN/pg_trgm index exists in the production DB.
findings.recommendedChange: Reframe the search strategy around SqlServerSearchProvider (STRING_SIMILARITY 2022+ / SOUNDEX+DIFFERENCE 2019). Mark pg_trgm/GIN as the non-production Postgres provider only, or remove it.

findings.location: Migration Dependency Graph (migrations 0001–0014)
findings.docSays: Lists an ordered migration dependency chain 0001 (Extensions/Search Setup) through 0014 (Debit Card Tables), implying a drizzle/numbered-migration workflow.
findings.actualState: No migrations/ or drizzle/ directory exists in the repo, and no 0001–0014 migration files exist anywhere. drizzle.config.ts targets Postgres (out: './migrations', dialect: 'postgresql') and is not applied to production. Production SQL Server schema is managed by standalone idempotent scripts under scripts/ (e.g. create_audit_event_table.sql, create_sessions_table.sql, create_performance_indexes.sql, ensure_rbac_provenance_columns.sql, widen_employee_last_seen_saml_role.sql) and Insert Queries/Schema Changes/*.sql.
findings.recommendedChange: Delete the fictional 0001–0014 migration graph. Replace with the actual change-management model: SQL Server schema is applied via standalone idempotent scripts under scripts/ and Insert Queries/Schema Changes/, not drizzle-kit migrations.

findings.location: Business Rule Enforcement Map — Database-Level Constraints (CUSTOMER, DEBIT_CARD sections)
findings.docSays: CUSTOMER has 'CHECK: customer_name_type_check' enforcing individual-vs-business name rules and a 'customer_full_name_trigger (PostgreSQL)'; DEBIT_CARD has 'CHECK: chk_expiry_month (1-12)' and 'CHECK: chk_expiry_year (≥ current year)'.
findings.actualState: These name/type and expiry rules are enforced in the Zod validation layer, not DB CHECK constraints: insertCustomerSchema is a z.discriminatedUnion on customerType (shared/schema.ts:906-929); expiry rules are in insertDebitCardSchema via z.number().min(1).max(12) and min(currentYear) (schema.ts:1117-1124). The only explicit CHECK constraint in shared/schema.ts is check_note_one_target on the note table (schema.ts:598-601), which the doc does not mention.
findings.recommendedChange: Correct the constraint map: attribute customer name/type and debit-card expiry rules to the Zod (application) layer unless a physical DB CHECK is verified in the SQL Server DDL. Add the note.check_note_one_target CHECK (exactly one of customer_id/account_id).

findings.location: Index Strategy Map — 'CUSTOMER SEARCH ... SQL Server: Full-text index on (first_name, last_name, full_name) — CONTAINS()'
findings.docSays: SQL Server customer search uses a full-text index with CONTAINS() and STRING_SIMILARITY() for fuzzy matching (SQL Server 2022).
findings.actualState: SqlServerSearchProvider does not use a full-text CONTAINS() index; it uses STRING_SIMILARITY() (2022+) or SOUNDEX/DIFFERENCE (2019) computed over full_name (SqlServerSearchProvider.ts:157,194). Production performance indexes are B-tree nonclustered (e.g. IX_customer_name on (last_name, first_name) in scripts/create_performance_indexes.sql), not full-text.
findings.recommendedChange: Remove the full-text CONTAINS() claim; describe the actual SQL Server fuzzy approach (STRING_SIMILARITY / SOUNDEX+DIFFERENCE) and the actual nonclustered indexes from create_performance_indexes.sql.

findings.location: DEBIT CARD box and Business Rule Enforcement — trigger descriptions ('PostgreSQL: BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger; SQL Server: FOR INSERT/UPDATE trigger with ROLLBACK')
findings.docSays: Debit-card account-type enforcement exists as a PostgreSQL BEFORE trigger and a SQL Server FOR trigger, and Summary Statistics claims 'Triggers: 2'.
findings.actualState: shared/schema.ts:433-450 states these are DB triggers 'in both PostgreSQL and SQL Server' but the trigger bodies are not present in schema.ts or the standalone scripts reviewed — only described in a comment. Only the SQL Server variant is production-relevant. The debit_card table also has a NOT NULL customer_id FK enforcing account-owner linkage (schema.ts:468), which the doc's debit_card box omits.
findings.recommendedChange: Drop the PostgreSQL trigger variant (non-production). State that the debit-card account-type / owner-validation rules are enforced by SQL Server triggers whose DDL is external to the reviewed files (cite location if found). Add customer_id (NOT NULL, → customer) and limit_profile_id to the debit_card box.

findings.location: CUSTOMER box — 'full_name ◄── Auto-generated (trigger/computed)'; and constraint map 'TRIGGER customer_full_name_trigger (PostgreSQL) / COMPUTED full_name (SQL Server)'
findings.docSays: full_name is auto-populated by a PostgreSQL trigger and a SQL Server persisted computed column.
findings.actualState: In shared/schema.ts, full_name is a plain varchar(200) column (schema.ts:114) that the Zod insertCustomerSchema omits as 'Generated column, not manually inserted' (schema.ts:902). Whether it is a physical computed column or trigger-maintained is not evidenced in schema.ts or the reviewed scripts; the PostgreSQL-trigger half is non-production.
findings.recommendedChange: Remove the PostgreSQL-trigger description. State that full_name is treated as a generated/derived column (omitted from inserts); confirm the exact SQL Server mechanism (computed column vs trigger vs app-populated) against the production DDL and cite it.

findings.location: Performance Monitoring Recommendations (SQL block) — 'PostgreSQL: Monitor table bloat ... FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname = public'

findings.recommendedChange: Remove the PostgreSQL monitoring query (or clearly mark it non-production). Keep and expand the SQL Server monitoring guidance.

docPurpose: Complete reference for every environment variable consumed by the ClientIQ / Banking Client 360 app, organized by functional category, with defaults, required/optional status, and a production example.
summary: The document is substantially inaccurate and reads like an idealized/aspirational config guide rather than a reflection of the actual codebase. A large fraction of the variables it documents (DB_POOL_*, SESSION_TIMEOUT, all SESSION_COOKIE_* except the hard-coded name, LOG_FORMAT, DEBUG, CORS_ORIGIN, RATE_LIMIT_*, ENABLE_AUDIT_LOGGING, ENABLE_PERFORMANCE_MONITORING, every "Optional SAML Setting", and all SAML_ATTR_* mapping overrides) are never read anywhere in the code. Meanwhile the document omits nearly all of the real variables the app actually consumes: SAML_ENABLED, SAML_ROLE_ENV, SAML_DEFAULT_ROLE_NAME, RSA_PORTAL_URL, DB_VENDOR, the DB_* fallback chain, and ROLE_TESTING_ENABLED. It also invents a dotenv-style .env file location (the app has no dotenv; config comes from PowerShell env exports) and a "[Config] validation" startup sequence that does not exist. It still frames PostgreSQL/DATABASE_URL as a first-class option and defaults DATABASE_DIALECT to postgresql, contrary to the SQL-Server-only ground rule.

findings.location: Configuration File Location
findings.docSays: Development: .env in project root; Production: C:\ClientIQ\config\.env
findings.actualState: The app does not use dotenv at all (no 'dotenv' dependency in package.json, no dotenv import in server/*.ts). Environment variables are set by PowerShell scripts that export process env before launching the app: Start-Dev.ps1 / Start-Server.ps1, and the pipeline-generated C:\ClientIQ\Start-Server.ps1 (facts/deployment.md; PipelineTemplates/start-script.yml). There is no C:\ClientIQ\config\.env and no .env loading of any kind.
findings.recommendedChange: Replace the '.env file location' framing entirely. Document that config is delivered via PowerShell env exports: dev via repo-root Start-Dev.ps1, and each server via the pipeline-generated C:\ClientIQ\Start-Server.ps1. State explicitly that the app does not read a .env file (no dotenv).

findings.location: SAML Configuration / Quick Reference
findings.docSays: SAML section lists only SAML_ENTRYPOINT, SAML_ISSUER, SAML_CALLBACK_URL, SAML_CERT plus a set of 'Optional' settings. It never mentions SAML_ENABLED.
findings.actualState: SAML_ENABLED is the master gate for all SSO (server/index.ts:21, server/middleware/authGate.ts:6, server/routes/auth.ts:19). It must be the exact string 'true' to enable SAML; when falsy, SAML is off (dev falls back to mock auth). All Start scripts set SAML_ENABLED=false; ADO sets it via $(SAMLEnabled). This is arguably the single most important auth variable and is entirely absent from the doc.
findings.recommendedChange: Add SAML_ENABLED as a required/primary SAML variable: Values 'true'/'false' (exact string 'true' enables SSO), default off. Explain the dev mock-auth fallback when it is not 'true'.

findings.location: SAML Configuration
findings.docSays: Does not document SAML_ROLE_ENV or SAML_DEFAULT_ROLE_NAME.
findings.actualState: SAML_ROLE_ENV scopes AD-group->role mapping to one environment (DEV/TST/STG/PRD); unset means AD groups from all environments are honored (server/auth/samlStrategy.ts:109,122; server/routes/auth.ts:362). It is set per ADO stage via SAMLRoleEnv (azure-pipelines.yml:110-234). SAML_DEFAULT_ROLE_NAME is the fallback role when no AD-group role matches, default 'Branch Manager' (server/auth/samlStrategy.ts:123; server/routes/auth.ts:357,416).
findings.recommendedChange: Add both variables. SAML_ROLE_ENV: optional, per-environment role scoping (DEV/TST/STG/PRD), default = all-environments mode. SAML_DEFAULT_ROLE_NAME: optional, default 'Branch Manager'.

findings.location: SAML Configuration / Optional SAML Settings
findings.docSays: Lists optional SAML settings SAML_LOGOUT_URL, SAML_LOGOUT_CALLBACK_URL, SAML_DECRYPT_KEY, SAML_SIGNATURE_ALGORITHM, SAML_DIGEST_ALGORITHM, SAML_CLOCK_SKEW_MS with defaults, and provides example values.
findings.actualState: None of these variables are read anywhere in the code (repo-wide grep for each returns zero process.env references). The real logout portal link is controlled by RSA_PORTAL_URL (server/routes/auth.ts:39), which the doc does not mention. Signature/digest/clock-skew behavior is not env-configurable in this codebase.
findings.recommendedChange: Delete the entire 'Optional SAML Settings' table (all six variables are non-functional). Replace with the one real logout-related variable, RSA_PORTAL_URL (optional; if unset, the logout origin is derived from SAML_ENTRYPOINT).

findings.location: SAML Configuration / Custom Attribute Mapping
findings.docSays: SAML_ATTR_EMPLOYEE_ID / _EMPLOYEE_NUMBER / _FIRST_NAME / _LAST_NAME / _EMAIL / _DEPARTMENT / _ROLE override default SAML attribute URIs, shown with urn:oid: values.
findings.actualState: No SAML_ATTR_* variable is read anywhere (grep returns nothing). The attribute mapping is a hard-coded constant ATTRIBUTE_MAP in server/auth/samlStrategy.ts:95-103 using http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/... claim URLs (not urn:oid:), and the verify callback primarily relies on short NameFormat=basic attribute names. Attribute mapping is not environment-configurable.
findings.recommendedChange: Remove the entire 'Custom Attribute Mapping' section (variables do not exist). If attribute mapping needs documentation, describe the hard-coded ATTRIBUTE_MAP and short-name resolution in samlStrategy.ts instead, and note it is code-level, not env-configurable.

findings.location: Database Configuration / DATABASE_DIALECT + PostgreSQL Variables
findings.docSays: DATABASE_DIALECT Default: postgresql, Values postgresql/postgres/pg/sqlserver/mssql. Presents a 'PostgreSQL Variables' table with DATABASE_URL as 'Required: Yes' when dialect is postgresql, and example DATABASE_URL=postgresql://...
findings.actualState: SQL Server is the only production engine. The default-postgresql behavior is real in code (server/dbConfig.ts:29 'Default to PostgreSQL') but contradicts the production ground rule; all Start scripts set DATABASE_DIALECT=sqlserver and DB_VENDOR=mssql. DATABASE_URL is NOT required at server runtime on the SQL Server path (defaults to '' in dbConfig.ts:12); it is only required by drizzle.config.ts (the drizzle-kit CLI, PG abstraction), which throws if unset (drizzle.config.ts:3).
findings.recommendedChange: State SQL Server is the only production engine and that deploys always set DATABASE_DIALECT=sqlserver. Demote the PostgreSQL/DATABASE_URL material to a clearly-labeled 'legacy PG abstraction (non-production)' note, and clarify DATABASE_URL is required only for the drizzle-kit CLI, not the running server.

findings.location: Database Configuration / Connection Pool Settings
findings.docSays: DB_POOL_MIN (default 2), DB_POOL_MAX (default 10), DB_POOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT (default 30000) configure the connection pool, with an example setting them to 5/20/60000.
findings.actualState: None of DB_POOL_MIN / DB_POOL_MAX / DB_POOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT are read anywhere (repo-wide grep returns zero matches). Pool sizes are hard-coded: main pool max:10, min:0, idleTimeoutMillis:30000 (server/dbConnection.ts:34-37); session store pool max:10, min:0, idleTimeoutMillis:30000 (server/auth/session.ts:20-24). Setting these env vars has no effect.
findings.recommendedChange: Delete the Connection Pool Settings section (variables are non-functional). If pool sizing must be documented, state the values are hard-coded (main and session pools: max 10, min 0, idle 30000 ms) and not env-tunable.

findings.location: Database Configuration / SQL Server Variables
findings.docSays: Documents MSSQL_SERVER, MSSQL_DATABASE, MSSQL_USER, MSSQL_PASSWORD, MSSQL_PORT, MSSQL_ENCRYPT, MSSQL_TRUST_SERVER_CERTIFICATE only.
findings.actualState: Missing the DB_* fallback chain and DB_VENDOR that the code actually uses. Each MSSQL_* connection var falls back to a DB_* equivalent: MSSQL_USER->DB_USER, MSSQL_PASSWORD->DB_PASSWORD, MSSQL_SERVER->DB_SERVER->'localhost', MSSQL_DATABASE->DB_NAME->'ClientIQ' (server/auth/session.ts:8-11; server/dbConnection.ts:23-26). DB_VENDOR (server/adapters/search/SearchProviderFactory.ts:25) selects the search provider ('mssql'); Start scripts set it. None are documented.
findings.recommendedChange: Add the DB_USER/DB_PASSWORD/DB_SERVER/DB_NAME fallback variables (optional; used only when the MSSQL_* equivalent is unset) and DB_VENDOR (optional; set to 'mssql' by deploy to select the SQL Server search provider).

findings.location: Database Configuration / SQL Server Variables (MSSQL_ENCRYPT, MSSQL_TRUST_SERVER_CERTIFICATE, MSSQL_PORT)
findings.docSays: MSSQL_ENCRYPT default true, MSSQL_TRUST_SERVER_CERTIFICATE default false, MSSQL_PORT default 1433 — presented as governing the SQL Server connection generally.
findings.actualState: MSSQL_ENCRYPT and MSSQL_TRUST_SERVER_CERTIFICATE are honored ONLY by the session store connection (server/auth/session.ts:15-16). The main data pool hard-codes encrypt:true and derives trust solely from NODE_ENV==='development' (server/dbConnection.ts:28-29), ignoring both vars. MSSQL_PORT is never read (no process.env.MSSQL_PORT in code); it is set by Start scripts but the mssql pool uses the default port regardless (facts/env-vars.md Section 2).
findings.recommendedChange: Clarify that MSSQL_ENCRYPT / MSSQL_TRUST_SERVER_CERTIFICATE affect only the session-store connection, while the main pool hard-codes encrypt:true and keys trust off NODE_ENV. Mark MSSQL_PORT as a set-but-unread (dead) variable, or remove it.

findings.location: Validation (Startup Validation + Missing Variables)
findings.docSays: Shows a '[Config] Validating environment configuration...' startup sequence and a '[Config] ERROR: Missing required environment variables' block claiming the app validates required vars on startup and refuses to start when they are missing.
findings.actualState: No such validation exists. Repo-wide grep for 'Validating environment', 'Environment validation complete', and 'Missing required environment variables' returns nothing. Required vars like SESSION_SECRET, SAML_CALLBACK_URL, and SAML_ENTRYPOINT are read with non-null assertions (server/auth/session.ts:34; server/auth/samlStrategy.ts:129-130) and would fail at use, not via a validation gate with these messages.
findings.recommendedChange: Delete the entire Validation section, or rewrite it to reflect reality: there is no config-validation gate; missing required vars fail at runtime (e.g., session signing or SAML strategy construction) rather than producing the documented '[Config]' messages.

findings.location: Application Settings / HOST
findings.docSays: HOST (default 0.0.0.0) sets the network interface to bind to.
findings.actualState: process.env.HOST is never read. The server hard-codes host '0.0.0.0' in its listen block (server/index.ts). HOST is exported by Start scripts (e.g., 127.0.0.1) but has no effect (facts/env-vars.md Section 2).
findings.recommendedChange: Remove HOST or mark it as a set-but-unread (dead) variable: the listen host is hard-coded to 0.0.0.0 regardless of HOST.

findings.location: Session Configuration (SESSION_TIMEOUT, SESSION_COOKIE_NAME, SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE)
findings.docSays: SESSION_TIMEOUT (default 3600000), SESSION_COOKIE_NAME (default clientiq.sid), and SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE (default true in production) are configurable session variables.
findings.actualState: None are read (grep returns zero matches). These values are hard-coded in server/auth/session.ts: cookie.maxAge = 60*60*1000 (1h), name = 'clientiq.sid', and secure = (NODE_ENV === 'production'). Only SESSION_SECRET is an actual env input (session.ts:34).
findings.recommendedChange: Remove SESSION_TIMEOUT, SESSION_COOKIE_NAME, and SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE as env variables. Note the values are hard-coded (1h idle with rolling refresh, cookie name clientiq.sid, secure derived from NODE_ENV).

findings.location: Logging Configuration (LOG_FORMAT, DEBUG)
findings.docSays: LOG_FORMAT (json/pretty, default json in production) and DEBUG (Node.js debug namespaces, e.g. passport:*,saml:*) control logging.
findings.actualState: Neither is read (grep returns zero matches for process.env.DEBUG and LOG_FORMAT). Only LOG_LEVEL is an actual logging input (server/services/loggerConfig.ts:7, consumed in server/services/logger.ts:140), default 'debug' in dev and 'info' otherwise. The app uses a custom/pino-style logger, not the Node 'debug' module keyed off DEBUG.
findings.recommendedChange: Remove LOG_FORMAT and DEBUG. Keep LOG_LEVEL but correct its default to 'debug' in development and 'info' otherwise (not a flat 'info').

findings.location: Security Settings (CORS_ORIGIN, RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS, RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS) and Feature Flags (ENABLE_AUDIT_LOGGING, ENABLE_PERFORMANCE_MONITORING)
findings.docSays: CORS_ORIGIN, RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS (default 60000), RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS (default 100), ENABLE_AUDIT_LOGGING (default true), and ENABLE_PERFORMANCE_MONITORING (default false) configure security and feature behavior.
findings.actualState: None of these five variables are read anywhere (repo-wide grep returns zero matches). The one real runtime feature flag the doc omits is ROLE_TESTING_ENABLED (server/services/roleTestService.ts:14; role-testing/impersonation enabled unless exactly 'false').
findings.recommendedChange: Delete the entire 'Security Settings' and 'Feature Flags' sections (all five variables are non-functional). Add the real feature flag ROLE_TESTING_ENABLED (optional; enabled unless set to exactly 'false').

findings.location: Application Settings / whole doc
findings.docSays: Runtime/logging variables covered: NODE_ENV, PORT, HOST, LOG_LEVEL (plus fabricated ones).
findings.actualState: Omits the app-controlled timezone behavior: server/utils/timezone.ts:13,20 forces TZ='America/Los_Angeles' (PST) at startup. TZ is set by the app, not operator-provided; documenting it prevents confusion about why process TZ is fixed.
findings.recommendedChange: Add a short note that the app forces process TZ to America/Los_Angeles at startup (server/utils/timezone.ts); TZ is not an operator input knob.

findings.location: Complete Production Example / Application (NODE_ENV=production)
findings.docSays: The production example sets NODE_ENV=production.
findings.actualState: The actual deploy pipeline writes NODE_ENV=development into the generated C:\ClientIQ\Start-Server.ps1 for ALL environments including prod (PipelineTemplates/start-script.yml; facts/deployment.md:201-204). Consequences: secure-cookie flag is false, main-pool trustServerCertificate is true, dev-only debug routes activate, and log level defaults to debug. Whether the Windows service overrides NODE_ENV to production is not visible in the repo.
findings.recommendedChange: Correct or flag this: the repo's deploy scripts set NODE_ENV=development in all environments. Either document that reality (and its security implications) or explicitly note that production NODE_ENV must be overridden at the service level, which cannot be confirmed from the repo.

findings.location: SAML Configuration / SAML_ISSUER + SAML_CERT
findings.docSays: SAML_ISSUER 'Required: Yes' (SP Entity ID); SAML_CERT 'Required: Yes' described only as 'IdP certificate (base64)'.
findings.actualState: SAML_ISSUER is effectively optional in code: the strategy defaults it to 'ClientIQ-Production' when unset (server/auth/samlStrategy.ts:128). SAML_CERT can be either an inline PEM (when the value contains 'BEGIN CERTIFICATE') or a file path that is read from disk (server/auth/samlStrategy.ts:16); deploy sets it to ./saml_cert.pem (start-script.yml).
findings.recommendedChange: Mark SAML_ISSUER optional (defaults to 'ClientIQ-Production'). For SAML_CERT, document the dual inline-PEM vs file-path behavior and that the deploy uses the file path ./saml_cert.pem.

findings.location: Security Best Practices (secret rotation, ownership) + plaintext secrets
findings.docSays: Advises never committing .env files, rotating secrets annually, and locking down .env file permissions.
findings.actualState: The repo commits plaintext secrets in Start-Dev.ps1 (MSSQL_PASSWORD line 16, SESSION_SECRET line 23), contradicting the 'never commit secrets' guidance (facts/env-vars.md notes). Rotation cadence/ownership and the prod secret-management process are governance items not verifiable from code.
findings.recommendedChange: Have a human owner confirm the secret-rotation policy and reconcile the guidance with the committed plaintext secrets in Start-Dev.ps1 (which should be removed/rotated). Note the actual secret delivery is via ADO variable groups ($(SessionSecret), $(DBPassword)), not .env files.

docPurpose: Operator runbook for obtaining/installing SSL/TLS certificates, configuring DNS, terminating TLS in Nginx on Windows in front of the ClientIQ app, and handling certificate renewal.
summary: The doc is a generic Nginx-on-Windows TLS/DNS runbook whose core premise is not supported by the repo: there is no Nginx (or IIS/web.config) configuration or reference anywhere in the codebase. The app is a Node/Express Windows Service listening on plain HTTP :5000; a TLS terminator is *expected* in front (SAML URLs are https), but its identity (Nginx vs IIS/ARR vs hardware LB) is not defined in this repo, so every C:\nginx path, nginx.conf snippet, and `nginx.exe` command is unverified and likely wrong for this environment. The hostname clientiq.fmb.com appears nowhere in code (only the IdP portal.fmb.com is real, and the SP host is the ADO variable $(SAMLHost)), and the health-check URL used for verification (/health) is not a registered route — the actual endpoint is /api/health. No PostgreSQL claims appear in this doc. Governance items (internal CA, DNS ownership, wildcard cert availability, HSTS rollout) are non-code and need human confirmation.

findings.location: Overview / Certificate Installation (Steps 1-6) / entire doc premise
findings.docSays:
TLS is terminated by Nginx on Windows: certificates live under C:
ginx\conf\ssl\, nginx.conf uses ssl_certificate/ssl_certificate_key, and you validate/reload with `.
ginx.exe -t` and `.
ginx.exe -s reload` (or Restart-Service Nginx).
findings.actualState: No Nginx config, nginx.conf, C:\nginx path, nginx.exe reference, or Nginx service exists anywhere in the repo (grep for 'nginx' across *.ts/*.js/*.yml/*.ps1/*.conf/*.md returns nothing; find -iname '*nginx*' returns nothing). The app is a Windows Service running `npx tsx watch server/index.ts` from C:\ClientIQ, listening on plain HTTP host 0.0.0.0 port 5000 (server/index.ts:98-101; PipelineTemplates/start-script.yml:48). deployment.md §5.2 states explicitly that no nginx/IIS/web.config is in the repo and warns 'do not claim nginx specifically.'
findings.recommendedChange: Do not assert Nginx. Reframe the doc as 'TLS termination in front of ClientIQ (reverse proxy — component TBD)'. State the verified facts: the Node app listens on plain HTTP :5000 and something external must terminate TLS. Mark the specific reverse-proxy product (Nginx vs IIS/ARR vs hardware LB) as needs-human-input and replace all C:\nginx\... paths and nginx.exe commands once the actual terminator is confirmed.

findings.location: DNS Configuration (A/CNAME records) and every certificate CN/SAN example (clientiq.fmb.com)
findings.docSays: Create an A record for clientiq.fmb.com pointing to the server IP, use CN/SAN = clientiq.fmb.com for the certificate, and browse to https://clientiq.fmb.com.
findings.actualState: The hostname 'clientiq.fmb.com' appears nowhere in the codebase (grep across ts/js/yml/ps1/json returns nothing). The only fmb.com hostname in the repo is the IdP portal.fmb.com used for SAML entrypoint/IdP-initiated URLs (PipelineTemplates/start-script.yml:33,36). The SP's own host is injected as the ADO pipeline variable $(SAMLHost) (SAML_CALLBACK_URL=https://$(SAMLHost)/saml/acs, start-script.yml:35), i.e. the real app FQDN is environment-specific and not hard-coded to clientiq.fmb.com.
findings.recommendedChange: Replace clientiq.fmb.com with a placeholder such as <app-fqdn> / $(SAMLHost) and note that the actual FQDN is the value bound to $(SAMLHost) per environment (dev/test/preprod/prod), which must match the certificate CN/SAN and the SAML_CALLBACK_URL. Confirm the real per-env FQDNs with the DNS/infra owner (needs-human-input).

findings.location: Verify SSL Configuration → Test with PowerShell (Invoke-WebRequest .../health)
findings.docSays: Health check: `Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://clientiq.fmb.com/health"` and expect a 200 StatusCode.
findings.actualState: There is no `/health` route registered in the app; the only health endpoint is `app.get("/api/health", ...)` returning {status:"healthy"} (server/routes.ts:3133-3135). `/health` is merely allowlisted in authGate (server/middleware/authGate.ts:16) but no handler serves it, so the request would fall through to the SPA catch-all or 404 rather than return a health JSON.
findings.recommendedChange: Change the verification URL to https://<app-fqdn>/api/health (the actual health route). Optionally note that /health is auth-allowlisted but not backed by a handler.

findings.location: Overview / Security Best Practices (secure cookies, forwarded headers)
findings.docSays: The doc never mentions that the app runs behind the TLS terminator on plain HTTP :5000, does not mention Express `trust proxy`, and does not note that the session secure-cookie flag depends on NODE_ENV.
findings.actualState: The session cookie `secure` flag is `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'` (server/auth/session.ts:41), but the ADO deploy launches every environment with NODE_ENV=development (PipelineTemplates/start-script.yml:16 per deployment.md §1.5/§4). Behind a TLS terminator this means secure cookies are OFF in deployed environments. There is also no `app.set('trust proxy', …)` and no X-Forwarded-Proto handling in server/index.ts / routes / auth (grep returns nothing), and no helmet/HSTS in the app.
findings.recommendedChange: Add an operator note that TLS terminates upstream and the app receives plain HTTP on :5000; call out that because deploys run NODE_ENV=development the session cookie `secure` flag is currently false and there is no trust-proxy/HSTS in the app, so HSTS and secure-cookie enforcement must be handled at the TLS terminator (or NODE_ENV/behavior fixed). Flag for security review.

findings.location: Overview: 'Certificate installation in Nginx' + Step 6 Reload Nginx (Restart-Service Nginx)
findings.docSays: Install the cert in Nginx and reload it (`.\nginx.exe -s reload` or `Restart-Service Nginx`); the app is fronted by an Nginx service named 'Nginx'.
findings.actualState: The only Windows Service defined by the deploy pipeline is the ClientIQ app service ($(serviceName), Start-Service/Stop-Service in PipelineTemplates/deploy-nodejs.yml:22,36); there is no evidence of an Nginx Windows Service. deployment.md §5.1 documents the app as a Windows Service in C:\ClientIQ launched via tsx watch, with no nginx/IIS layer in the repo.
findings.recommendedChange: Remove the assumed `Restart-Service Nginx` / nginx.exe reload steps or gate them behind 'if your environment uses Nginx as the terminator (confirm with infra)'. Document the actual known service: the ClientIQ app Windows Service under C:\ClientIQ.

findings.location: Certificate Options (Option 1 internal CA, Option 3 wildcard) / Renewal Process ownership
findings.docSays: Request certs from your internal PKI/security team; a *.fmb.com wildcard may be available; renewal SLA is 30/14/7 days with alerts to ops@fmb.com.
findings.actualState: These are governance/ownership facts (internal CA existence, wildcard availability, renewal ownership, alert distribution) that cannot be verified from the repo. The repo only shows the app expects HTTPS externally (SAML https URLs) and a SAML signing cert at ./saml_cert.pem (start-script.yml:37); it says nothing about the server TLS cert issuance process or the ops@fmb.com alias.
findings.recommendedChange: Confirm with the security/PKI and DNS owners: internal CA process, whether a *.fmb.com wildcard is issued, the correct per-environment FQDNs, and the real renewal/alert distribution list. Mark these sections as owner-confirmed rather than assumed.

findings.location: Overview / any 'related config' section
findings.docSays: The doc covers only DNS, cert issuance, Nginx install, and renewal; it does not mention the SAML signing certificate or the app's own TLS-relevant env context.
findings.actualState: Separate from the server TLS cert, the app loads a SAML IdP signing certificate from SAML_CERT (default './saml_cert.pem' relative to C:\ClientIQ) — inline PEM if it contains 'BEGIN CERTIFICATE', else a file path (server/auth/samlStrategy.ts:16; start-script.yml:37; env-vars.md §1). This is a distinct certificate operators frequently confuse with the TLS cert.
findings.recommendedChange: Add a short 'Not the same as the TLS certificate' note distinguishing the server TLS/SSL cert (this doc) from the SAML signing cert (saml_cert.pem, SAML_CERT env var), cross-linking the SAML auth setup doc.

docPurpose: Step-by-step operator guide for installing and running the ClientIQ / Banking Client 360 Node app on a Windows Server host (Node install, app dir, env config, Windows service, firewall, log rotation, verification, troubleshooting).
summary: The guide is substantially out of date with how the app is actually built, deployed, and run. Its two load-bearing premises are wrong: (1) it describes running the compiled production build (dist/server/index.js) as a hand-installed NSSM/node-windows service with NODE_ENV=production, but the real ADO pipeline deploys via PowerShell Remoting and runs the app from TypeScript source with npx tsx watch and NODE_ENV=development; and (2) it says the app runs behind an Nginx reverse proxy, but there is no Nginx anywhere in the repo. Multiple concrete details are also false: the build emits dist/index.js + dist/public (not dist/server + dist/client), the health endpoint returns a different shape, and the .env example lists nonexistent/dead env vars while omitting real ones. Nothing about SQL Server being production is wrong, but the deployment/runtime mechanics need a near-total rewrite.

findings.location: Overview
findings.docSays: The application runs as a Node.js service behind Nginx reverse proxy.
findings.actualState: No nginx config, reference, or service exists anywhere in the repo (azure-pipelines.yml, PipelineTemplates/*.yml, Start-*.ps1, server/*). The only reverse proxy in the codebase is the in-app Express Streamlit proxy at /streamlit (server/proxy.ts). TLS termination in front of the Node app is expected (SAML uses https, app listens plain http:5000 at server/index.ts) but is not defined in this repo, and is not confirmed to be nginx.
findings.recommendedChange: Remove the specific 'behind Nginx reverse proxy' claim. State that the Node app listens on plain HTTP port 5000 and that an external TLS terminator/reverse proxy (technology unspecified/managed outside this repo) is expected in front. Do not name nginx unless confirmed by ops.

findings.location: Step 5: Install Windows Service (NSSM AppParameters 'dist/server/index.js'; node-windows script 'C:\ClientIQ\app\dist\server\index.js')
findings.docSays: Install a Windows service that runs node.exe with parameters 'dist/server/index.js' (or node-windows pointing at C:\ClientIQ\app\dist\server\index.js), i.e. the compiled server at dist/server/index.js.
findings.actualState: The esbuild build bundles server/index.ts to a single file dist/index.js (package.json build: '--outdir=dist', entry server/index.ts) — there is no dist/server/ directory. Moreover the actual ADO deploy does not run the compiled bundle at all: PipelineTemplates/start-script.yml launches 'npx tsx watch --clear-screen=false server/index.ts' from TypeScript source (start-script.yml:48).
findings.recommendedChange: Correct the compiled path to dist/index.js if documenting the npm-production path. But more importantly, document that the sanctioned pipeline runtime runs from source via 'npx tsx watch server/index.ts', not a compiled dist file — reconcile the guide with the actual deploy model (see PipelineTemplates).

findings.location: Step 5 (NODE_ENV=production) / Step 8 (production runtime assumptions)
findings.docSays: Service runs with NODE_ENV=production (nssm set ClientIQ AppEnvironmentExtra 'NODE_ENV=production'; node-windows env NODE_ENV=production).
findings.actualState: The ADO-generated C:\ClientIQ\Start-Server.ps1 sets NODE_ENV=development for ALL environments (start-script.yml:16). Consequence: the deployed server uses the Vite dev middleware path (server/index.ts branch on app.get('env')==='development', server/vite.ts), mock/dev auth unless SAML_ENABLED=true (server/index.ts:56-61), secure-cookie disabled, main-pool trustServerCertificate=true, and debug log level. This is a real dev/prod mismatch, not production mode.
findings.recommendedChange: Either document that the pipeline currently runs NODE_ENV=development (and its implications for auth/static serving/logging/cookies), or, if the guide's intent is a true production install, flag prominently that this diverges from the actual pipeline. Do not present NODE_ENV=production as the deployed reality.

findings.location: Step 3: Verify File Structure (dist\client and dist\server)
findings.docSays: dist\ contains client\ (Frontend assets) and server\ (Backend compiled code).
findings.actualState: Vite outputs client assets to dist/public (vite.config.ts:20, outDir dist/public), and esbuild outputs the server bundle to dist/index.js (package.json:8). serveStatic serves 'public' relative to the bundled server (server/vite.ts:65). There is no dist/client or dist/server directory.
findings.recommendedChange: Update the file-structure tree to dist\public\ (frontend assets) and dist\index.js (server bundle). Remove dist\client and dist\server.

findings.location: Step 8: Test Application Health (expected response)
findings.docSays: GET /api/health expected response: { "status": "ok", "timestamp": "...", "database": "connected" }.
findings.actualState: server/routes.ts:3133-3139 returns { status: "healthy", timestamp: <ISO>, service: "Banking Customer API" }. There is no 'database' field and status is 'healthy', not 'ok'. The endpoint does not check DB connectivity. authGate allowlists '/health' exact (server/middleware/authGate.ts:16), while /api/health falls under the /api handling.
findings.recommendedChange: Correct the expected response to { status: 'healthy', timestamp: '...', service: 'Banking Customer API' } and remove the implication that health reflects database connectivity.

findings.location: Step 5: Install Windows Service (entire NSSM / node-windows manual procedure)
findings.docSays: Manually install the Windows service on the box using NSSM (download from nssm.cc, nssm install ClientIQ ...) or node-windows (install-service.js), pointing at node.exe + dist path.
findings.actualState: Deployment is done by the Azure DevOps pipeline over PowerShell Remoting: deploy-nodejs.yml copies the artifact to C:\ClientIQ, then Stop-Service/Start-Service the existing Windows service named $(serviceName) (deploy-nodejs.yml:16-38), and start-script.yml regenerates C:\ClientIQ\Start-Server.ps1 remotely. The service already exists on the host and runs the generated start script; the guide's manual NSSM/node-windows setup does not match the tsx-watch/source runtime the pipeline configures.
findings.recommendedChange: Rewrite this section to reflect the ADO PowerShell-Remoting deploy (copy artifact -> stop service -> optional npm ci -> start service) and the generated Start-Server.ps1 that launches 'npx tsx watch server/index.ts'. If NSSM is genuinely how the service was originally created, keep only the one-time service-creation steps and align AppParameters/AppDirectory/env with the real runtime; otherwise treat this whole section as obsolete.

findings.location: Step 4: Create Environment Configuration (.env + Step 5 DOTENV_CONFIG_PATH)
findings.docSays: Create C:\ClientIQ\config\.env and point the service at it via DOTENV_CONFIG_PATH=C:\ClientIQ\config\.env.
findings.actualState: The app never reads DOTENV_CONFIG_PATH; there is no dotenv config wiring in the deploy path. Env is set inline by the generated C:\ClientIQ\Start-Server.ps1 (start-script.yml sets $env:* directly before launching tsx) and by Start-Dev.ps1/Start-Server.ps1 at repo root. grep of the codebase shows no process.env.DOTENV_CONFIG_PATH consumer.
findings.recommendedChange: Replace the .env + DOTENV_CONFIG_PATH approach with the actual mechanism: env vars are exported inline by the (pipeline-generated or repo-root) Start-Server.ps1 PowerShell script that then runs tsx. If a .env file is desired, document how it would actually be loaded, but note the current code/pipeline does not use one.

findings.location: Step 4: Environment file — SAML block (SAML_LOGOUT_URL)
findings.docSays: SAML_LOGOUT_URL=https://idp.yourbank.com/saml/logout is part of the env configuration.
findings.actualState: No code reads SAML_LOGOUT_URL (grep across server/ and PipelineTemplates finds no process.env.SAML_LOGOUT_URL). Logout origin is derived from RSA_PORTAL_URL or SAML_ENTRYPOINT (server/routes/auth.ts:34-52). The real SAML env vars consumed are SAML_ENABLED, SAML_ENTRYPOINT, SAML_ISSUER, SAML_CERT, SAML_CALLBACK_URL, SAML_ROLE_ENV, SAML_DEFAULT_ROLE_NAME, RSA_PORTAL_URL.
findings.recommendedChange: Remove SAML_LOGOUT_URL. If documenting logout config, reference RSA_PORTAL_URL / SAML_ENTRYPOINT-derived origin instead.

findings.location: Step 4: Environment file — Database + SAML sections
findings.docSays: DB section lists DATABASE_DIALECT, MSSQL_SERVER/DATABASE/USER/PASSWORD/PORT, MSSQL_ENCRYPT, MSSQL_TRUST_SERVER_CERTIFICATE; SAML section lists ENTRYPOINT/ISSUER/CALLBACK_URL/LOGOUT_URL/CERT.
findings.actualState: The example omits several vars the real deploy sets/needs: DB_VENDOR=mssql (required for SearchProviderFactory to select SQL Server, else defaults to Postgres — server/adapters/search/SearchProviderFactory.ts:23-49), SAML_ROLE_ENV (per-env AD-group scoping, DEV/TST/STG/PRD — samlStrategy.ts/adGroupRoleMap.ts), SAML_DEFAULT_ROLE_NAME (default 'Branch Manager'), and RSA_PORTAL_URL. It also omits SAML_ENABLED itself (the master switch, server/index.ts:21).
findings.recommendedChange: Add DB_VENDOR=sqlserver alongside DATABASE_DIALECT=sqlserver (both are independent switches, both default to Postgres if unset), and add SAML_ENABLED, SAML_ROLE_ENV, SAML_DEFAULT_ROLE_NAME, and RSA_PORTAL_URL to the SAML section with their meanings.

findings.location: Step 4: Environment file — MSSQL_PORT / MSSQL_ENCRYPT / MSSQL_TRUST_SERVER_CERTIFICATE
findings.docSays: MSSQL_PORT=1433; MSSQL_ENCRYPT=true; MSSQL_TRUST_SERVER_CERTIFICATE=false control the DB connection.
findings.actualState: MSSQL_PORT is a dead var — no process.env.MSSQL_PORT reader exists; the mssql pool uses the default port (env-vars facts §2). MSSQL_ENCRYPT and MSSQL_TRUST_SERVER_CERTIFICATE are honored ONLY by the session store (server/auth/session.ts:15-16); the MAIN data pool hard-codes encrypt:true and derives trustServerCertificate solely from NODE_ENV==='development' (server/dbConnection.ts:28-29), ignoring both vars. The actual deploy sets MSSQL_ENCRYPT=false and MSSQL_TRUST_SERVER_CERTIFICATE=true (start-script.yml:26-27), the opposite of the doc's true/false.
findings.recommendedChange: Note MSSQL_PORT has no effect (default 1433 used regardless). Clarify that MSSQL_ENCRYPT/MSSQL_TRUST_SERVER_CERTIFICATE affect only the session store; the main pool's encryption is fixed (encrypt=true) and its cert trust follows NODE_ENV. Align example values with the actual deploy or explicitly mark them as recommended-but-not-what-pipeline-sets.

findings.location: Step 6: Configure Firewall (only lists inbound 5000 and outbound 1433)
findings.docSays: Allow inbound on 5000 (localhost) and outbound to SQL Server on 1433.
findings.actualState: The app makes additional outbound connections not covered: SAML to the RSA IdP over https (portal.fmb.com / SAMLHost, start-script.yml:32-36) and an in-app Streamlit reverse proxy hard-coded to https://pyt-tstapp01.fmb.com (server/routes.ts:3150). A firewall that only allows 1433 outbound would block SSO and the /streamlit feature.
findings.recommendedChange: Add outbound rules for HTTPS (443) to the RSA IdP host and to the Streamlit host (pyt-tstapp01.fmb.com), or document these as required egress. Note the Streamlit target is currently hard-coded in server/routes.ts.

findings.location: Step 3: Deploy Application Files (npm ci --production)
findings.docSays: Install production dependencies with 'npm ci --production'.
findings.actualState: The app is run via tsx from TypeScript source (needs dev deps like tsx/vite at runtime because the deployed server uses the Vite dev middleware path under NODE_ENV=development — server/index.ts:88-92, start-script.yml:16,48). The pipeline runs 'npm ci --prefer-offline' (no --production) and only when the commit message contains 'npm ci' (azure-pipelines.yml:59, deploy-nodejs.yml:25-32). A production-only install would omit tsx/vite and break the deployed runtime.
findings.recommendedChange: Remove '--production' (or change to a full 'npm ci'), since the runtime depends on tsx/vite (dev dependencies). Document the pipeline's commit-message-gated 'npm ci' behavior and that node_modules is excluded from the build artifact.

findings.location: Step 4: SAML_CERT=MIIDxTCCA... (base64/DER-looking inline value)
findings.docSays: SAML_CERT is set to a bare base64 blob (MIIDxTCCA...).
findings.actualState: loadSamlCert() treats SAML_CERT as inline PEM only if it contains 'BEGIN CERTIFICATE'; otherwise it is treated as a FILE PATH and read from disk (server/auth/samlStrategy.ts:16-38), and it validates BEGIN/END markers. A bare base64 blob without PEM markers would be treated as a path and fail. The actual deploy sets SAML_CERT=./saml_cert.pem (a file path) (start-script.yml:37).
findings.recommendedChange: Show SAML_CERT either as a full PEM (with -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- markers) or as a file path (e.g. ./saml_cert.pem placed under C:\ClientIQ). Note the inline-vs-path detection hinges on the BEGIN CERTIFICATE marker.

findings.location: Step 3: Extract Application Package (clientiq-v2.0.0.zip)
findings.docSays: Deploy package clientiq-v2.0.0.zip (implies app version 2.0.0).
findings.actualState: package.json version is 1.0.0 (name 'rest-express'). The ADO artifact is named $(Build.Repository.Name), not a versioned clientiq-v2.0.0.zip (azure-pipelines.yml PublishBuildArtifacts). The 2.0.0 filename appears to be illustrative and does not match repo versioning.
findings.recommendedChange: Use a version-agnostic package name or align with the actual artifact naming (repository name) / package.json version (1.0.0). Mark the filename as an example if kept.

findings.location: Step 6: Firewall inbound rule (-LocalAddress 127.0.0.1 for port 5000)
findings.docSays: Restrict inbound 5000 to LocalAddress 127.0.0.1 (loopback only), implying the app binds to localhost.
findings.actualState: The server hard-codes listen host '0.0.0.0' (server/index.ts listen block); the HOST env var (set to 127.0.0.1 in start scripts) is never read (env-vars facts §2). So the process actually binds all interfaces; the firewall rule is what restricts exposure, which is consistent with the code comment that port 5000 'is the only port that is not firewalled'.
findings.recommendedChange: Clarify that the app binds 0.0.0.0 in code and that host-level exposure is controlled by this firewall rule (not by an app-level bind or the HOST env var, which is inert). Keep the loopback restriction but state why it matters.

docPurpose: System architecture reference for ClientIQ / Banking Client 360 — deployment topology, layered component architecture, data/ETL pipeline, security model (SAML SSO + RBAC/ABAC), database schema, technology stack, and CI/CD for FMB engineering, security, and architecture stakeholders.
summary: ClientIQ_Architecture_V2.2 is broadly the right shape (on-prem Windows, SQL Server, RSA SAML, React/Express, Notes, RBAC/ABAC) but wrong on many load-bearing specifics: it claims SQL Server Full-Text Search (CONTAINS/CONTAINSTABLE) when production uses case-insensitive LIKE; it invents an Nginx reverse proxy, a dev→UAT→prod / develop-uat-main pipeline, blue-green deploys, and SSIS stored-procedure ETL that do not exist (real deploy is ADO develop/test/preprod/prod branches, tsx-watch from source with NODE_ENV=development, PowerShell-remoting to a Windows Service, manual SQL-file ETL from Jack Henry views); and it gets schema/session/permission details wrong. The enterprise-architecture.txt blueprint is far more divergent — an aspirational, largely fictional design (dual PostgreSQL+SQL Server, Redis, Kubernetes/HPA, RabbitMQ, OAuth2/OIDC via Okta/Azure AD, circuit breakers, CQRS materialized views, event sourcing, multi-region DR, OFAC/AML) contradicting the single-engine SQL Server reality and the SAML/RSA auth; treat it as obsolete for this system. The logical diagram (6.29.26) is the most accurate artifact and matches real infra. Headline problems: PostgreSQL/dual-database and trigram claims, Full-Text Search claim, wrong pipeline/branch/deploy model, and non-existent tables/constraints/permissions.

findings.location: enterprise-architecture.txt — Executive Summary; Part 2.3 Data Architecture (Dual Vendor Strategy); Part 3.1 Adapter Pattern; ADR-001
findings.docSays: 'supporting dual-database deployment (PostgreSQL and Microsoft SQL Server)'; 'Vendor Neutrality: Database-agnostic design'; PostgresSearchProvider uses pg_trgm trigram similarity; separate /migrations/postgres/ and /migrations/sqlserver/ dirs; ADR-001 'switch databases without code changes.'
findings.actualState: SQL Server is the ONLY production engine. server/dbConnection.ts is 'MS SQL Server only'; getPgDatabase() throws 'not available — this deployment uses MS SQL only' (dbConnection.ts:74-79). The PostgresSearchProvider/pg_trgm path exists in the abstraction but is never the production engine (frontend-ui.md §4; db-schema.md §1.1). There is no /migrations/postgres/ vs /migrations/sqlserver/ split; drizzle.config targets Postgres only and is not applied to prod (db-schema.md §11).
findings.recommendedChange: Remove all dual-database / vendor-neutral / PostgreSQL / pg_trgm-trigram framing. State that SQL Server is the sole production engine; note the residual Drizzle-pg abstraction (pgTable schema, drizzle-kit) exists only for type generation and is not a supported second runtime engine. Delete ADR-001's 'switch databases without code changes' claim.

findings.location: ClientIQ_Architecture_V2.2 — 1.1/1.2 (Search & Discovery), 3.1 Data Access Layer, 4.2 Full-Text Search Configuration, 4.4/5.3
findings.docSays: 'Intelligent fuzzy search powered by SQL Server Full-Text Search with relevance ranking'; a 'SQL Server Full-Text Search Provider' with CONTAINS() queries, CONTAINSTABLE() relevance ranking, and FULLTEXT INDEX ON customer(full_name) WITH CHANGE_TRACKING AUTO.
findings.actualState: Production search is case-insensitive substring LIKE with COLLATE Latin1_General_CI_AS across first_name/last_name/business_name/full_name/tax_identifier/silverlake_customer_id and CONCAT(first,last) — server/storage/sqlServerCustomerSearch.ts:42-43,103-120. There is no CONTAINS/CONTAINSTABLE/FULLTEXT usage anywhere (grep returns none); no relevance ranking (frontend-ui.md §4).
findings.recommendedChange: Replace the entire Full-Text Search section (4.2) and all 'FTS/CONTAINS/relevance ranking' references with the actual model: case-insensitive LIKE substring matching via COLLATE Latin1_General_CI_AS over the listed columns, no relevance score, provider selected by SearchProviderFactory (SqlServerSearchProvider).

findings.location: ClientIQ_Architecture_V2.2 — 6.2/6.3 Deployment & CI/CD; enterprise-architecture.txt — Part 7 CI/CD
findings.docSays: Environments Development/UAT/Production; pipeline triggers on develop/uat/main; 'Merge uat to main branch'; blue-green zero-downtime deploy via xcopy to \\prod-app02 + sc.exe restart 'Client360Service'; enterprise doc adds GitHub Actions, Docker, Kubernetes/Helm, k6, canary 10/50/100.
findings.actualState: Azure DevOps pipeline triggers on develop/test/preprod (prod not in trigger block), stages Deploy_Dev/Deploy_Test/DAST_Scan/Deploy_Preprod/Deploy_Prod/Deploy_Prod2 keyed to develop/test/preprod/prod — no uat or main branch anywhere (deployment.md §1.1-1.3). Deploy is PowerShell-Remoting: copy artifact → Stop-Service → optional npm ci → Start-Service (deployment.md §1.6). No blue-green, Kubernetes, Docker, Helm, k6, or GitHub Actions. Prod deploys to two servers (Deploy_Prod + Deploy_Prod2). Per project memory, preprod/prod deploy from ADO branches, NOT GitHub main.
findings.recommendedChange: Rewrite environments and CI/CD to the real four-branch ADO model (develop→Dev, test→Test[+OWASP ZAP DAST], preprod→PreProd, prod→Prod on two servers), PowerShell-remoting Windows-Service deploy, SonarQube SAST on develop only. Remove UAT/uat/main, blue-green, Kubernetes, Docker, Helm, GitHub Actions. Add that pushing GitHub main does not reach preprod/prod.

findings.location: enterprise-architecture.txt — whole document (Parts 2-8: Redis, Kubernetes/HPA, RabbitMQ/Kafka, OAuth2/OIDC, circuit breakers, CQRS, event sourcing, multi-region DR, OFAC/AML)
findings.docSays: Redis session/query cache, Kubernetes cluster with HPA (3-10 API pods), RabbitMQ/Kafka queue, OAuth2/OIDC IdP (Okta/Azure AD) with JWT Bearer tokens, circuit breakers for Jack Henry/Silverlake REST, CQRS materialized views, event_store event sourcing, active-active multi-region DR (Traffic Manager/Route 53), OFAC/AML/SAR workflows.
findings.actualState: None of this is in the codebase. Auth is RSA SAML 2.0 via @node-saml/passport-saml (saml-ad.md), not OAuth2/OIDC/JWT/Okta/Azure AD. Sessions are SQL Server-backed (connect-mssql-v2), not Redis; no Redis, Kubernetes, RabbitMQ/Kafka, circuit breaker, CQRS materialized views, event_store table, or multi-region DR exists. No OFAC/AML/SAR/compliance-alert features or tables (no compliance_alert in shared/schema.ts). App runs as a single Windows Service via tsx watch.
findings.recommendedChange: Do not use enterprise-architecture.txt as the architecture source of truth — it is an aspirational blueprint that contradicts the implementation. Retire it, or clearly mark every unbuilt element (Redis, K8s, RabbitMQ, OAuth2/OIDC, circuit breakers, CQRS, event sourcing, multi-region DR, OFAC/AML) as 'future/not implemented'. Consolidate onto ClientIQ_Architecture_V2.2 corrected per these findings.

findings.location: ClientIQ_Architecture_V2.2 — 1.1/1.3/1.4/2.1/6.x Nginx reverse proxy; enterprise-architecture.txt — security zones/ingress
findings.docSays: 'Nginx reverse proxy for SSL termination and load balancing' (HA pair), TLS 1.3 termination at Nginx, round-robin/sticky sessions, /health checks; enterprise doc uses NGINX Ingress Controller in Kubernetes.
findings.actualState: No Nginx (or IIS/web.config) config exists anywhere in the repo (deployment.md §5.2-5.3). The Node app listens on plain HTTP port 5000 bound 0.0.0.0 (server/index.ts). A TLS terminator is expected in front (SAML URLs are https) but is not defined in-repo — the logical diagram shows load-balanced app servers (CIQ-APP01/02) without naming Nginx. The only in-repo reverse proxy is the app's Express Streamlit proxy at /streamlit (server/proxy.ts).
findings.recommendedChange: Remove specific 'Nginx' claims (TLS termination, LB algorithm, health-check specifics) unless FMB ops confirms Nginx. State the app listens HTTP:5000 and an external TLS terminator/load balancer fronts it (per the logical diagram's CIQ-APP01/02) — product unspecified in-repo. Flag for human input to confirm the actual proxy.

findings.location: ClientIQ_Architecture_V2.2 — 4.3/4.4 Core Data Models & Schema; enterprise-architecture.txt — 2.3 ERD
findings.docSays: CREATE TABLE customer with customer_type NOT NULL DEFAULT 'individual' and CONSTRAINT CK_customer_name_type CHECK((individual AND first/last) OR (business/trust/estate AND business_name)); ERD lists debit_card.limit_profile_id FK to DEBIT_CARD_LIMIT_PROFILE.
findings.actualState: customer_type default is 'regular', not 'individual' (shared/schema.ts:122). There is NO CK_customer_name_type CHECK constraint — the only DB CHECK is note.check_note_one_target (shared/schema.ts:598; db-schema.md §13). Name/type validation is Zod discriminated union over individual|premium|regular|business|trust (no 'estate') (shared/schema.ts:907-929). Debit-card rules are enforced by DB triggers, not a check constraint; production SQL Server debit_card carries inline limit columns, not a limit_profile_id FK — only the faker/dev path uses a debit_card_limit_profile FK model (data-seed.md §5.2).
findings.recommendedChange: Correct customer_type default to 'regular'; remove the fabricated CK_customer_name_type constraint (validation is Zod-based over individual/premium/regular/business/trust, not 'estate'). Note the debit-card limit divergence (inline columns in SQL Server vs FK profile in the dev seed).

findings.location: ClientIQ_Architecture_V2.2 — 4.4 SQL Server Session Store; 3.1/4.1 Session Store; 7.1 auth flow (24-hour TTL)
findings.docSays: sessions table with columns session_id/session_data/expires_at/created_at + usp_cleanup_expired_sessions stored proc; '24-hour TTL'; cookie 'Secure' with 24-hour session.
findings.actualState: The real sessions table (connect-mssql-v2) has sid NVARCHAR(255) PK, session NVARCHAR(MAX), expires DATETIME (scripts/create_sessions_table.sql; db-schema.md §11.2) — not session_id/session_data/expires_at, and there is no usp_cleanup_expired_sessions proc (auto-removes expired rows every 15 min). Session TTL is 12 hours, not 24 (session.ts:30); cookie maxAge is 1h idle with rolling refresh, sameSite:'lax' (secure only in production), cookie name clientiq.sid (session.ts:39-45; saml-ad.md §4.4).
findings.recommendedChange: Update the session store schema to sid/session/expires (connect-mssql-v2), remove the invented cleanup stored proc (note 15-min auto-remove), and correct TTL to 12h with a 1h rolling idle cookie, sameSite=lax, cookie name clientiq.sid.

findings.location: ClientIQ_Architecture_V2.2 — 2.2/4.1/4.5 ETL (SSIS/stored procs, staging tables, daily 2:00 AM); enterprise-architecture.txt — batch processing
findings.docSays: App DB populated via SSIS/SQL Agent ETL: stg_customer/stg_account/stg_transaction staging tables and usp_load_customers/usp_load_accounts/usp_load_transactions/usp_load_households stored procs with MERGE UPSERT, daily delta at 2:00 AM.
findings.actualState: The actual SQL Server ETL is hand-run SQL files under 'Insert Queries/*.sql' that load ClientIQPreProd.dbo.* directly from Jack Henry views (TheSpot/TheSpotPreProd/TheVault), run manually in FK order with no orchestrator (data-seed.md §1, §5). No stg_* staging tables, no usp_load_* stored procedures, and no evidence of a 2:00 AM SSIS delta schedule in the repo. financial_transaction.sql loads only the last 13 months and pivots joins on account_number (data-seed.md §5.2; db-schema.md §5).
findings.recommendedChange: Replace the SSIS/staging-table/stored-proc narrative with the real flow: manually executed Insert Queries/*.sql loading from Jack Henry TheSpot/TheVault views into ClientIQPreProd, FK-ordered, idempotent via MERGE/NOT EXISTS, 13-month transaction window. Flag the SSIS orchestration/2AM schedule as unverified unless FMB confirms an out-of-repo SSIS job.

findings.location: ClientIQ_Architecture_V2.2 — 1.4/7.1 Security (Every API request validated; branch ABAC as the model); notes gating
findings.docSays: 'Permission Enforcement: Every API request validated against user permissions'; ABAC example 'Branch restriction (employee.branchId = customer.branchId)' presented as the model.
findings.actualState: Not every route is permission-gated: Notes (all CRUD) and deposit-summary/deposit-trend endpoints are authentication-only with NO requirePermission and NO notes.* permission exists anywhere (rbac.md §7.1; grep for notes.* returns none). The seeded ABAC permission is transaction.view with an employee-customer restriction (customer.isEmployee requires priv ≥3), evaluated in the PG permissionService; the SQL Server store instead implements branch/region restrictions and the PG ABAC check no-ops when db is null — so the employee-record ABAC may not fire in production (rbac.md §5.4, §11.3).
findings.recommendedChange: Soften 'every request validated' and document the gaps (Notes and deposit-summary/trend are auth-only; no notes.* permission). Document the real ABAC: seeded transaction.view employee-customer restriction (priv ≥3) plus a divergent SQL Server branch/region model, and flag that the two ABAC implementations disagree (potential prod gap).

findings.location: ClientIQ_Architecture_V2.2 — 5.1 Backend Technologies table; 3.1 API Layer (npm saml); connection pool
findings.docSays: SAML library 'npm saml' (Latest); 'Password Hashing bcryptjs 3.0.2 — Secure password storage'; mssql 12.0.0; connection pooling 'max 100 connections'.
findings.actualState: SAML is @node-saml/passport-saml ^5.1.0 (package.json:22), not a package called 'npm saml'. There is no password storage or bcrypt usage in server code (grep for bcrypt returns nothing) — auth is SSO-only via SAML, so 'password hashing' does not apply. The MSSQL pool is max:10 (server/dbConnection.ts:35), not 100.

docPurpose: Operator/support runbook for diagnosing and resolving ClientIQ (Banking Client 360) runtime issues across app, reverse proxy, database, SAML auth, and performance, with health checks, log locations, and escalation contacts.
summary: The guide is substantially out of date because it describes an architecture that does not match the repo. Its two biggest problems are (1) an entire Nginx reverse-proxy section (502/504/SSL, upstream config, C:\nginx\logs) with zero basis in the codebase — no nginx config, service, or reference exists anywhere — and (2) a runtime model built on a compiled Windows service (nssm, node dist/server/index.js, NODE_ENV=production) when the app actually deploys as a PowerShell-launched `npx tsx watch server/index.ts` process running from TypeScript source with NODE_ENV=development. Log paths, service-restart commands, the manual-start command, the health endpoint path, and the SAML signature/attribute guidance are all wrong or unverifiable. It contains no explicit PostgreSQL claim (the DB sections are correctly SQL Server), but many concrete commands would fail as written and would mislead an operator during an incident.

findings.location: Nginx Issues (502 Bad Gateway, 504 Gateway Timeout, SSL Certificate Errors) + Quick Diagnostics / Log Locations references to Nginx
findings.docSays: A full 'Nginx Issues' section: Get-Service -Name "Nginx", nginx upstream 'clientiq_backend { server 127.0.0.1:5000; }', C:\nginx\logs\clientiq_access.log / clientiq_error.log / error.log, nginx.conf 'location /api/' proxy_read_timeout, and SSL cert files at C:\nginx\conf\ssl\clientiq.crt.
findings.actualState: There is NO nginx config, nginx reference, or nginx service anywhere in the repo (verified: grep for nginx across *.ts/*.yml/*.ps1/*.json/*.conf returns nothing; deployment.md §5.2 states this explicitly). The app listens on plain HTTP 0.0.0.0:5000 (server/index.ts:98-102) and some external TLS terminator is expected but is NOT nginx-specific and is not configured in this repo.
findings.recommendedChange: Do not name Nginx. Rename the section to 'Reverse Proxy / TLS Terminator (external)' and state the front-end proxy is provisioned outside this repo; remove the Get-Service -Name Nginx, upstream block, nginx.conf snippets, and C:\nginx\logs paths unless a real infra doc confirms nginx is the chosen terminator. Flag for human confirmation of what actually fronts port 5000.

The compiled entry, when built, is `dist/index.js` (package.json:8), never `dist/server/index.js`. So `node dist/server/index.js` points at a path that does not exist. Deploy install uses `npm ci --prefer-offline` gated on the commit message containing 'npm ci' (deploy-nodejs.yml:25-32), not `npm ci --production`.
findings.recommendedChange: Change the manual-start command to `npx tsx server/index.ts` (or `tsx watch ...`) from C:\ClientIQ, matching the deploy. Correct the module-not-found remedy to `npm ci` (note node_modules is excluded from the artifact and only reinstalled when the commit message says 'npm ci').

findings.location: SAML Authentication Issues > Invalid Signature ('Verify signature algorithm matches (SHA-256 required)')
findings.docSays: Signature errors are fixed by ensuring the signature algorithm is SHA-256 (required), implying assertion signatures are validated.
findings.actualState: The strategy sets signatureAlgorithm 'sha256' (samlStrategy.ts:140) BUT wantAssertionsSigned=false and wantAuthnResponseSigned=false (samlStrategy.ts:138-139) because RSA SecurID signs the Response wrapper, not the Assertion; passport-saml accepts whichever element is signed. audience=false and validateInResponseTo=never (samlStrategy.ts:142-143). So 'signature validation failed' is far more likely a cert mismatch (SAML_CERT) than an algorithm mismatch, and the doc's framing of assertion-signature enforcement is misleading.
findings.recommendedChange: Reframe: primary cause of signature failures is a stale/wrong IdP cert in SAML_CERT. Note the SP does not require the assertion to be signed (Response-wrapper signing per RSA), signatureAlgorithm is sha256, and audience/InResponseTo validation are disabled. Point operators at the startup cert log (SHA-256 fingerprint, validFrom/validTo) that samlStrategy.ts emits.

Logging is via the app's own structured logger controlled by LOG_LEVEL and NODE_ENV (loggerConfig.ts:6-7; logger.ts:140). The strategy already emits detailed startup diagnostics and per-login SAML logs unconditionally.
findings.recommendedChange: Replace the DEBUG=passport:*,saml:* tip with `set LOG_LEVEL=debug` (or rely on NODE_ENV=development, which the deploy already uses). Note the app logs SAML attribute extraction and role sync details on its own.

docPurpose: A database-design reference for data engineers: the ClientIQ / Banking Client 360 SQL Server schema — table definitions, relationships, indexes, constraints, triggers, and common query patterns.
summary: The design doc is broadly correct on the shape of the core banking tables (customer, account, financial_transaction, household, junction tables) and correctly targets SQL Server DDL, but it is undermined by a pervasive "PostgreSQL parity / dual-database" framing that violates the ground rule that SQL Server is the only production engine. Several concrete claims are now false: full_name is described as a PERSISTED computed column (it is a plain ETL-populated varchar), account carries a sic_code column + FK (it does not — SIC is a junction table), financial_transaction.account_id is shown NOT NULL (it is nullable and the ETL now pivots on account_number, which the doc omits), and financial_transaction has a debit_card_id FK/index that does not exist on the table. The audit relies on a "Migration History 0001-0014" and full-text-catalog DDL that have no backing files in the repo (no migrations/, drizzle/, or full-text scripts). Whole domains present in the real schema are missing from the detailed doc: the entire Notes module, the full RBAC/audit table set, region, and the SIC junction tables. The two source artifacts also disagree with each other (39 vs a different real count; overview shows employee SSO fields the detailed DDL drops).

findings.location: database-design-sqlserver.md — Overview / Design Principles, and 'PostgreSQL Parity Notes' section (lines 26, 30, 1236-1251)
findings.docSays: "The SQL Server implementation maintains complete parity with the PostgreSQL version..." and lists 'Dual-Database Parity: Functionally equivalent to PostgreSQL implementation'; an entire closing 'PostgreSQL Parity Notes' section compares pg_trgm/PL-pgSQL/BIGSERIAL to SQL Server equivalents.
findings.actualState: SQL Server is the only production engine. The runtime pool is MSSQL-only (server/dbConnection.ts:1-4,49-52); getPgDatabase() throws 'not available — this deployment uses MS SQL only' (server/dbConnection.ts:74-79). The pg abstraction (shared/schema.ts pgTable, drizzle.config dialect=postgresql) is non-production tooling, not a live parallel database.
findings.recommendedChange: Remove the dual-database / PostgreSQL-parity framing. Reframe as a single SQL Server design. Keep at most a short note that shared/schema.ts is authored in Drizzle pgTable for type generation only, and that production DDL is SQL Server. Delete the 'PostgreSQL Parity Notes' section.

findings.location: database-design-sqlserver.md — customer table DDL, 'Computed Columns', 'Performance Considerations' (lines 88-98, 147-153, 1054-1065); overview .txt line 175

findings.actualState: full_name is a plain nullable column: fullName: varchar("full_name", { length: 200 }) (shared/schema.ts:114-115), populated by the ETL as a literal value (Insert Queries/customer.sql:9 inserts full_name directly). No PERSISTED/computed-column DDL exists anywhere in the repo (grep for PERSISTED / 'full_name AS' returns nothing).
findings.recommendedChange: Change full_name to a plain VARCHAR(200) NULL column and state it is populated by the SQL Server ETL / application on write, not a computed column. Remove the PERSISTED computed-column DDL and the 'Computed Columns' feature claims.

docPurpose: EPIC/feature/user-story technical requirements spec for the ClientIQ / Banking Client 360 customer-360 CRM, defining data model, search, RBAC, compliance, and infrastructure behavior across 9 EPICs.
summary: The document is structurally sound (the 9 EPICs map to real domains: customers, accounts, debit cards, transactions, search, households, compliance, branch/employee, infrastructure), but its cross-cutting architecture claims are substantially outdated. Its single largest defect is the "dual-database" / PostgreSQL framing: the doc repeatedly presents Postgres trigram search, pg_trgm/GIN indexes, DB_VENDOR-driven runtime provider swapping, and vendor-parallel migration directories as first-class production behavior, when SQL Server is the only production engine and the runtime is hard-wired to MSSQL. Several concrete facts are simply wrong: the customer name rule is a Zod discriminated-union in app code (not a DB CHECK constraint `customer_name_type_check`), production customer search is plain case-insensitive LIKE (not trigram/STRING_SIMILARITY/SOUNDEX), and the "8 named debit-card limit profiles" only exist in the non-production faker seed. Many EPIC 7 (SAR/OFAC/dispute), EPIC 3 (activation/PIN/replacement-fee) and EPIC 9 (health endpoint, migration dirs, rollback scripts) requirements describe features with no code backing. Roughly two-thirds of the load-bearing technical assertions need correction or removal.

findings.location: Header / Stack line (line 6) and Document Overview (line 12)
findings.docSays: Stack: React.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL/SQL Server, Material Design ... acceptance criteria aligned with the dual-database enterprise architecture.
findings.actualState: SQL Server is the only production engine. The runtime connection manager is MSSQL-only (server/dbConnection.ts:1-4, :49-52) and the PostgreSQL helpers are stubs that throw (getPgDatabase() throws 'not available — this deployment uses MS SQL only', server/dbConnection.ts:74-79). Postgres remains only as a residual abstraction (pgTable in shared/schema.ts, drizzle.config dialect=postgresql).
findings.recommendedChange: Change the stack to 'Microsoft SQL Server (production)' and drop the 'dual-database enterprise architecture' framing. Optionally add a one-line note that a residual PostgreSQL/Drizzle abstraction exists in the repo for type generation and dev tooling but is not a production runtime.

findings.location: EPIC 9: Dual-Database & Infrastructure (entire EPIC, lines 912-1018)
findings.docSays: Database-agnostic architecture supporting both PostgreSQL and Microsoft SQL Server ... Runtime Vendor Detection: Automatic provider selection via DB_VENDOR env var; SearchProviderFactory returns appropriate provider; 'Provider swap requires zero code changes'.
findings.actualState: The runtime data layer (server/dbConnection.ts) is hard-wired to SQL Server and ignores the vendor detectors entirely. Two independent detectors exist (DATABASE_DIALECT in server/dbConfig.ts:11-30 and DB_VENDOR in SearchProviderFactory.ts:23-49), both DEFAULTING to Postgres when unset — production must explicitly set DATABASE_DIALECT=sqlserver AND DB_VENDOR=mssql. There is no live Postgres runtime path; provider 'swap' is not a supported production capability.
findings.recommendedChange: Rewrite EPIC 9 as a SQL-Server-only infrastructure EPIC. Remove 'automatic vendor detection / zero-code provider swap' as a product requirement, or demote it to a note that the code carries an unused abstraction defaulting to Postgres. Document the real deployment reality (Windows Service in C:\ClientIQ, tsx watch, Azure DevOps branch-based deploy).
