findings.location: EPIC 1 Data Model line 27, US-1.2.2 (lines 84-90), EPIC 5 (lines 526-625), EPIC 9 US-9.3.1/9.3.2 (lines 977-994)
findings.docSays: Search Support: PostgreSQL trigram similarity, SQL Server STRING_SIMILARITY/SOUNDEX ... PostgreSQL uses trigram similarity (default 30%); SQL Server 2022+ uses STRING_SIMILARITY; SQL Server <2022 falls back to SOUNDEX; 'Smyth' finds 'Smith' with ~33% similarity.
findings.actualState: Production global customer search is plain case-insensitive substring LIKE with COLLATE Latin1_General_CI_AS across first_name/last_name/business_name/full_name/tax_identifier/silverlake_customer_id and CONCAT(first,last) (server/storage/sqlServerCustomerSearch.ts:103-126). trigram/similarity()/SOUNDEX/STRING_SIMILARITY only appear in the non-production abstraction (server/storage.ts PG paths, server/adapters/search/PostgresSearchProvider.ts, and a parallel SqlServerSearchProvider that is not the wired production search). There is no relevance-score fuzzy matching or 30% threshold in the production LIKE path.
findings.recommendedChange: Rewrite the search acceptance criteria to describe SQL Server case-insensitive LIKE substring matching as the production behavior. Remove trigram/pg_trgm/GIN and the '33%/37% similarity' examples, or clearly label them as pertaining to the dormant Postgres abstraction only. Note that a SqlServerSearchProvider with STRING_SIMILARITY exists in an adapter but is not what the production customer-search endpoint runs.

findings.docSays: PostgresSearchProvider: Uses pg_trgm trigram similarity and GIN indexes; pg_trgm extension enabled; GIN indexes created on first_name, last_name, business_name; migrations in /migrations/postgres/ and /migrations/sqlserver/ with matching numbers; rollback scripts available for each migration.
findings.actualState: Production SQL Server schema is managed by standalone idempotent .sql scripts under scripts/ and 'Insert Queries/Schema Changes/' plus manual DDL — NOT by drizzle-kit (which targets Postgres) and NOT by paired /migrations/postgres + /migrations/sqlserver directories (db-schema.md §11; deployment facts). No pg_trgm/GIN indexes are used in production; those are Postgres-abstraction-only. No numbered rollback-script scheme is evidenced.
findings.recommendedChange: Remove pg_trgm/GIN index requirements and the /migrations/postgres + /migrations/sqlserver paired-directory model. Document the actual SQL Server DDL-script workflow (create_audit_event_table.sql, create_sessions_table.sql, create_performance_indexes.sql, ensure_*_role/provenance scripts, widen_*_saml_role, Insert Queries/Schema Changes/*). findings.docSays: The doc omits the actual implemented RBAC/audit/SAML compliance machinery and instead lists SAR/OFAC/AML features.

No SAR-to-FinCEN, OFAC-list, or AML-threshold code exists.
findings.recommendedChange: Add an EPIC/section documenting the real RBAC + audit + SAML compliance implementation (roles, permissions, privilege levels, ABAC employee-record rule, audit_event taxonomy, permission_denial_log). docPurpose: Operator/admin guide for configuring SAML 2.0 SSO between ClientIQ (SP) and the RSA IdP: SP env-var setup, IdP metadata/attribute release, role synchronization, custom attribute mapping, testing, security settings, and troubleshooting.
summary: The doc is structurally sound and the SP env-var basics (SAML_ENTRYPOINT, SAML_ISSUER, SAML_CALLBACK_URL, SAML_CERT) plus the RSA-IdP framing are correct, but multiple core sections are materially wrong or invented. The biggest defect is role assignment: the doc presents the saml_role_mapping DB table with initial/enforced sync modes as THE login-time mechanism, but that table is dormant (its processSamlRole is never called) and the real login path is a convention-based AD-group-name mapping (adGroupRoleMap.ts) that the doc never mentions. Several documented env vars do not exist in code (SAML_ATTR_* overrides, SAML_DECRYPT_KEY, SAML_LOGOUT_URL, SAML_LOGOUT_CALLBACK_URL, SESSION_TIMEOUT), and concrete config values (NameID format, wantAssertionsSigned, clock skew, one endpoint path) contradict the code. saml_role_mapping is also a pgTable, so the table/SQL examples reflect the non-production PG abstraction.

findings.location: Step 4: Role Mapping — 'SAML Role Mapping Table' / 'Sync Modes' / 'Configure Role Mappings'
findings.docSays: ClientIQ assigns roles on login via the saml_role_mapping table, which maps IdP roles to app roles with sync_mode 'initial' (first login only) or 'enforced' (synced every login), configured by INSERTing rows into saml_role_mapping.
findings.actualState: saml_role_mapping is dormant on the login path. Its service method processSamlRole (server/services/samlRoleMappingService.ts:48) is never called anywhere (grep shows only its own definition). The live ACS login flow instead calls the convention-based mapAdGroupsToRoleNames (server/routes/auth.ts:364, server/auth/adGroupRoleMap.ts:130) which maps AD *group names* to roles; the saml_role_mapping table is reached only via admin CRUD routes (/api/admin/saml-mappings).
findings.recommendedChange: Rewrite Step 4 to document the real mechanism: convention-based AD-group→role mapping in server/auth/adGroupRoleMap.ts. Explain the group naming convention <PREFIX>_<ENV>_APP_ClientIQ_<RoleToken>_<Access>, the token→role map (appadmin/appsvcs→System Admin, branchmanager→Branch Manager, teller→Teller, etc.), the enforced revoke-on-login behavior (AD-derived rows with assigned_by IS NULL are revoked when the group disappears; admin-granted rows are never touched), and SAML_ROLE_ENV scoping. Demote saml_role_mapping to an 'admin-managed table not currently driving login' note.

findings.location: Step 4 / whole document (no mention of AD-group convention or SAML_ROLE_ENV)
findings.docSays: Role assignment is driven entirely by explicit saml_role_mapping rows; there is no mention of AD group names, a group naming convention, environment scoping, or a default-role fallback.
findings.actualState: The actual login role sync depends on (a) the AD group naming convention parsed by CLIENTIQ_GROUP_RE in server/auth/adGroupRoleMap.ts:64, (b) SAML_ROLE_ENV env scoping (server/auth/adGroupRoleMap.ts:78-163; server/routes/auth.ts:362) so one on-prem AD serving all envs resolves to the right per-env role, and (c) a two-tier default-role safety net defaulting to 'Branch Manager' via SAML_DEFAULT_ROLE_NAME (server/routes/auth.ts:357,416; server/storage/sqlServerEmployee.ts ensureEmployeeHasDefaultRoleSqlServer).
findings.recommendedChange: Add sections documenting the AD group convention, the SAML_ROLE_ENV variable (values DEV/TST/STG/PRD, aliases PreProd→STG etc., unset=all-envs), and SAML_DEFAULT_ROLE_NAME with its 'never strand an authenticated user' behavior.

findings.location: Step 5: Custom Attribute Mapping — 'Override via Environment Variables' (SAML_ATTR_EMPLOYEE_ID, SAML_ATTR_FIRST_NAME, ... SAML_ATTR_ROLE)
findings.docSays: You can customize attribute names without code changes by setting SAML_ATTR_EMPLOYEE_ID, SAML_ATTR_EMPLOYEE_NUMBER, SAML_ATTR_FIRST_NAME, SAML_ATTR_LAST_NAME, SAML_ATTR_EMAIL, SAML_ATTR_DEPARTMENT, SAML_ATTR_ROLE.
findings.actualState: No such env vars exist. grep for SAML_ATTR_ in server/ returns nothing. ATTRIBUTE_MAP is a hardcoded const (server/auth/samlStrategy.ts:95-103) and the verify callback reads short names first then these fixed long-form URIs (samlStrategy.ts:159-165) — it is not env-overridable.
findings.recommendedChange: Remove the 'Override via Environment Variables' subsection entirely, or replace it with the truth: attribute URIs are hardcoded in ATTRIBUTE_MAP and changing them requires a code edit. Also note RSA sends short attribute names (NameFormat=basic) which are tried before the long-form URIs.

findings.location: Step 2: Environment Variables — SAML_LOGOUT_URL, SAML_LOGOUT_CALLBACK_URL, SAML_DECRYPT_KEY
findings.docSays: Set SAML_LOGOUT_URL (IdP logout URL), SAML_LOGOUT_CALLBACK_URL (logout callback), and optionally SAML_DECRYPT_KEY (private key for assertion decryption).
findings.actualState: None of these env vars are read by code (grep for SAML_LOGOUT_URL / SAML_LOGOUT_CALLBACK_URL / SAML_DECRYPT_KEY / decryptionPvk in server/ returns nothing). The SAML strategy (server/auth/samlStrategy.ts:127-151) has no logoutUrl or decryptionPvk option. Logout target is derived from RSA_PORTAL_URL / SAML_ENTRYPOINT (server/routes/auth.ts:38-52), and the logout callback is the fixed route /saml/logout/callback (auth.ts:523).
findings.recommendedChange: Remove SAML_LOGOUT_URL, SAML_LOGOUT_CALLBACK_URL, and SAML_DECRYPT_KEY from the env-var block. Document the actual logout config: RSA_PORTAL_URL (optional, must be https:, else derived from SAML_ENTRYPOINT origin, final fallback https://portal.fmb.com/WebPortal/) and the fixed /saml/logout and /saml/logout/callback routes. Note assertion decryption is not supported.

findings.location: Security Considerations — 'Signature Verification'
findings.docSays: ClientIQ requires signed assertions: signatureAlgorithm: 'sha256', digestAlgorithm: 'sha256', wantAssertionsSigned: true.
findings.actualState: wantAssertionsSigned is false and wantAuthnResponseSigned is false (server/auth/samlStrategy.ts:138-139). RSA SecurID Access signs the Response wrapper, not the Assertion, so both are false and passport-saml accepts whichever element is signed (samlStrategy.ts:135-137). There is no digestAlgorithm option set; signatureAlgorithm is 'sha256' (samlStrategy.ts:140).
findings.recommendedChange: Correct to wantAssertionsSigned: false and wantAuthnResponseSigned: false, and explain that RSA signs the Response wrapper (at least one signed element is required). Remove the nonexistent digestAlgorithm line, or verify it before documenting.

findings.location: Security Considerations — 'Audience Restriction' and 'Clock Skew'
findings.docSays: The application validates the audience in SAML assertions matches the configured issuer. A 5-minute clock skew tolerance is configured: acceptedClockSkewMs: 5 * 60 * 1000.
findings.actualState: Audience validation is DISABLED: audience: false (server/auth/samlStrategy.ts:143). Clock skew is 10 seconds, not 5 minutes: acceptedClockSkewMs: 10000 (samlStrategy.ts:144). Also validateInResponseTo is set to never (samlStrategy.ts:142).
findings.recommendedChange: Change 'Audience Restriction' to state audience restriction is currently NOT validated (audience:false). Correct clock skew to 10000 ms (10s). Optionally add that validateInResponseTo is disabled.

findings.location: SAML Endpoints Reference — 'Session' row (/api/auth/session)
findings.docSays: Session endpoint: GET /api/auth/session — Check current session.
findings.actualState: No /session route exists. The session/status endpoint is GET /api/auth/status (server/routes/auth.ts:183), which reports isAuthenticated, employeeId, email, isLinked, samlEnabled, defaultRoleMissing.
findings.recommendedChange: Change the endpoint path from /api/auth/session to /api/auth/status and update the description to list the fields it returns (including isLinked and defaultRoleMissing).

findings.location: Security Considerations — 'Session Security' (SESSION_TIMEOUT)
findings.docSays: Session timeout configurable via SESSION_TIMEOUT environment variable.
findings.actualState: No SESSION_TIMEOUT env var exists (grep returns nothing). Session lifetime is hardcoded: cookie maxAge 60*60*1000 (1h idle, rolling refresh) and store ttl 12h (server/auth/session.ts:30,39). The only session-related env var is SESSION_SECRET (session.ts:34).
findings.recommendedChange: Remove the SESSION_TIMEOUT claim. State that idle timeout is a hardcoded 1-hour rolling cookie and the server-side store TTL is 12h, changeable only in code. Keep SESSION_SECRET as the one required session env var.

findings.location: Step 3: Configure IdP — 'Or provide manually' table (NameID Format) and Step 1 example; Example SAML Assertion
findings.docSays: NameID Format = urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress (and the example assertion uses the emailAddress NameID format).
findings.actualState: The SP is configured with identifierFormat: 'urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:persistent' (server/auth/samlStrategy.ts:133). Email is resolved from the emailaddress attribute or falls back to profile.nameID (samlStrategy.ts:163), but the requested NameID format sent in metadata is persistent, not emailAddress.
findings.recommendedChange: Update the NameID Format value to urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:persistent to match samlStrategy.ts:133, or explicitly document the mismatch and which one the IdP should honor.

findings.location: Step 4: Role Mapping — saml_role_mapping table definition and INSERT/SELECT SQL examples
findings.docSays: Presents saml_role_mapping as a plain relational table and gives raw INSERT/SELECT SQL (INSERT INTO saml_role_mapping (...) VALUES (...); SELECT ... JOIN role r ...) as the configuration method.
findings.actualState: saml_role_mapping is declared as a pgTable (shared/schema.ts:728) — part of the PostgreSQL/Drizzle abstraction, not the SQL Server production path — and it is dormant on login (see the obsolete-section finding). Production is SQL Server only (MSSQL_* env, sqlServerEmployee.ts); role assignment on login does not read this table.
findings.recommendedChange: If saml_role_mapping is retained in the doc at all, flag it as a Drizzle/PG-abstraction, admin-managed table not used at login, and note the syntax shown is generic and may differ on SQL Server. Prefer removing the SQL examples in favor of documenting the AD-group convention.

findings.location: SAML Endpoints Reference — 'Login' row (/api/auth/saml/login) and Step 6 'Test Login Flow' ('Sign In with SSO')
findings.docSays: Login endpoint GET /api/auth/saml/login 'Initiates SSO'; test flow says click 'Sign In with SSO'.
findings.actualState: /saml/login (mounted at both / and /api/auth) does call passport.authenticate('saml') for SP-initiated login (server/routes/auth.ts:256), but the actual primary login is GET /api/auth/login which renders a static sign-in page linking to the RSA portal, because RSA only emits a SAMLResponse when the user launches the ClientIQ tile from the portal (auth.ts:122-153,138-142). There is no 'Sign In with SSO' button flow that directly starts SSO from within the app.
findings.recommendedChange: Clarify the two entry points: /api/auth/login renders a static page directing users to click the ClientIQ tile in the RSA portal (SP-initiated /saml/login redirect does not by itself produce a login with this IdP). Update the test-flow wording to reflect launching from the RSA portal tile rather than an in-app 'Sign In with SSO' button.

findings.location: Step 2: Environment Variables (missing RSA_PORTAL_URL, SAML_ROLE_ENV, SAML_DEFAULT_ROLE_NAME, SESSION_SECRET, SAML_ENABLED)
findings.docSays: The .env block lists only SAML_ENTRYPOINT, SAML_ISSUER, SAML_CALLBACK_URL, SAML_LOGOUT_URL, SAML_LOGOUT_CALLBACK_URL, SAML_CERT, SAML_DECRYPT_KEY.
findings.actualState: Real, code-consumed SAML/auth env vars missing from the block: RSA_PORTAL_URL (server/routes/auth.ts:39), SAML_ROLE_ENV (adGroupRoleMap/auth.ts:362), SAML_DEFAULT_ROLE_NAME (auth.ts:357,416), the required SESSION_SECRET (server/auth/session.ts:34), and the master switch SAML_ENABLED (server/index.ts:21).
findings.recommendedChange: Add SAML_ENABLED, RSA_PORTAL_URL, SAML_ROLE_ENV, SAML_DEFAULT_ROLE_NAME, and SESSION_SECRET (required) to the environment-variable section with their purposes and defaults, and drop the nonexistent vars.

findings.location: Architecture / Overview and Prerequisites — 'SLO URL' and SP-initiated logout emphasis
findings.docSays: Lists an SLO (Single Logout) URL as an IdP item and frames SP-initiated logout as a first-class configured flow.
findings.actualState: Logout exists (GET /saml/logout calls strategy.logout, then destroys the session; server/routes/auth.ts:494-521) but there is no SAML_LOGOUT_URL config; the logout redirect target derives from RSA_PORTAL_URL/SAML_ENTRYPOINT. If the strategy has no logout, it just destroys the session and redirects to SPA_LOGIN_PATH.
findings.recommendedChange: Keep SLO in prerequisites but note it is optional and that ClientIQ derives the logout redirect from RSA_PORTAL_URL/SAML_ENTRYPOINT rather than a dedicated logout URL env var; a missing IdP logout capability degrades to local session destroy.

findings.location: Troubleshooting — 'User Not Created/Updated' ('Check employeeId is numeric and valid')
findings.docSays: For user-not-created issues, check employeeId is numeric and valid.
findings.actualState: Employee resolution keys on sso_subject/email then employee_number, and employee_number is derived (samlEmployeeNumber ?? samlEmployeeId ?? email-local-part, sliced to 20, final fallback SAML-<timestamp>) — auto-creation does not require a valid numeric employeeId (server/routes/auth.ts:322-343; server/storage/sqlServerEmployee.ts upsertEmployeeFromSamlSqlServer). docPurpose: Step-by-step guide for standing up a ClientIQ dev/test instance on a Windows Server (dev-mode Node app via tsx, SQL Server backend, nginx reverse proxy + TLS, run as a Windows service via NSSM).
summary: The doc is directionally correct on the big picture (Windows Server host, SQL Server backend, tsx-run dev mode, NSSM Windows service, C:\ClientIQ app root, port 5000) and correctly avoids Postgres. However, it is built around an nginx reverse proxy that does not exist anywhere in this repo, and it gets several concrete, copy-pasteable details wrong: the production build output path (dist/server/index.js vs actual dist/index.js), the SAML ACS/callback URL (/api/auth/saml/acs vs actual top-level /saml/acs), SAML_CERT format (claims base64, code wants inline PEM or a file path), and it documents several env vars the code never reads (SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE, LOG_FORMAT, HOST, MSSQL_PORT) while setting MSSQL_ENCRYPT=true where the deploy path uses false. It also omits any database migration/seed step and the DB_VENDOR var. A reader following it verbatim would misconfigure SAML and the production-mode build, and would build nginx plumbing the app's real deploy pipeline (Azure DevOps PowerShell remoting) does not use.

findings.location: Nginx Configuration for test-clientiq.fmb.com (Steps 1-4); Target Environment (Nginx: C:\nginx, SSL under C:\nginx\conf\ssl)
findings.docSays: Directs the reader to install nginx as a Windows service, place SSL certs under C:\nginx\conf\ssl\, and create nginx.conf + conf.d/test-clientiq.conf that reverse-proxies to the Node app on 127.0.0.1:5000. Presents nginx as the required front-end / TLS terminator.
findings.actualState: No nginx config, service, or reference exists anywhere in the repo (deployment.md §5.2/§6; verified across azure-pipelines.yml, PipelineTemplates/*.yml, Start-*.ps1, server/*). The real deploy path is Azure DevOps PowerShell remoting that copies the artifact and runs the app as a Windows service (PipelineTemplates/deploy-nodejs.yml). The app listens plain HTTP on 0.0.0.0:5000 (server/index.ts:99-102); TLS termination in front is expected but not defined in this repo; facts explicitly say do not claim nginx specifically.
findings.recommendedChange: Reframe the reverse-proxy/TLS section as environment-specific and NOT part of the app repo. State that ClientIQ itself only listens on HTTP :5000 and that TLS termination / reverse proxy (nginx, IIS/ARR, or other) is an infra decision configured outside this repo. Either drop the prescriptive nginx.conf blocks or clearly label them as an optional example that must be validated against the actual test environment.

findings.location: Running as a Windows Service > Option B: Build and Run Production Mode (AppParameters "dist/server/index.js")
findings.docSays: nssm set ClientIQ-Test AppParameters "dist/server/index.js" to run the compiled production server after npm run build.
findings.actualState: The build script bundles the server to dist/index.js, not dist/server/index.js: esbuild ... server/index.ts --outdir=dist and npm start runs node dist/index.js (package.json:8-9; deployment.md §2). There is no dist/server/index.js.

findings.location: Step 4: Create Environment Configuration (.env SAML block) and Nginx site config (location /api/auth/saml/)
findings.docSays: SAML_CALLBACK_URL=https://test-clientiq.fmb.com/api/auth/saml/acs, and nginx has a dedicated location /api/auth/saml/ block for SAML endpoints.
findings.actualState: The SAML ACS route is mounted at top-level /saml/acs, not under /api/auth (server/routes/auth.ts:264 router.post('/saml/acs'); the deploy template sets SAML_CALLBACK_URL=https://$(SAMLHost)/saml/acs, start-script.yml; deployment.md §5.4). The authGate allowlist references /saml/* and /IdPServlet, not /api/auth/saml.
findings.recommendedChange: Correct the callback URL to https://test-clientiq.fmb.com/saml/acs and change the proxy location from /api/auth/saml/ to /saml/. Cross-check SAML_ENTRYPOINT/IdP-initiated URLs against the portal.fmb.com/IdPServlet convention used in the deploy template.

findings.location: Step 4 .env comment: # SAML_CERT=your-test-idp-certificate-base64
findings.docSays: SAML_CERT is a base64-encoded IdP certificate.
findings.actualState: loadSamlCert() treats SAML_CERT as either inline PEM (if it contains 'BEGIN CERTIFICATE') or a filesystem path to a .pem file read from disk; it is not base64-decoded (server/auth/samlStrategy.ts:11-28). The deploy template sets SAML_CERT=./saml_cert.pem, i.e. a path (start-script.yml; deployment.md §5.4).
findings.recommendedChange: Describe SAML_CERT as either inline PEM content or a path to a .pem file (e.g. ./saml_cert.pem placed in C:\ClientIQ), not base64.

findings.location: Step 4 .env: SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=true and LOG_FORMAT=pretty
findings.docSays: Lists SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=true and LOG_FORMAT=pretty as configuration knobs.
findings.actualState: Neither variable is read anywhere in the codebase (grep of server/ and shared/ returns no matches). Secure-cookie behavior is derived from NODE_ENV in server/auth/session.ts (secure=false under development), and log formatting is controlled by loggerConfig/logger, not LOG_FORMAT. LOG_LEVEL is real (loggerConfig.ts:7).
findings.recommendedChange: Remove SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE and LOG_FORMAT (they are no-ops), or explicitly mark them as unused. Note the cookie secure flag follows NODE_ENV; keep LOG_LEVEL.

findings.location: All env-var blocks: HOST=127.0.0.1 and MSSQL_PORT=1433; Troubleshooting > ENOTSUP (set HOST=127.0.0.1)
findings.docSays: Sets HOST=127.0.0.1 and MSSQL_PORT=1433 and, in the ENOTSUP troubleshooting section, claims setting HOST=127.0.0.1 makes the app bind to localhost.
findings.actualState: process.env.HOST is never read; server.listen hard-codes host: '0.0.0.0' (server/index.ts:101). MSSQL_PORT is also never read; the mssql pool uses the default port (env-vars.md §2, dead vars). So setting HOST cannot change the bind address and would not fix an ENOTSUP on 0.0.0.0.
findings.recommendedChange: Flag HOST and MSSQL_PORT as set-but-unused. Rewrite the ENOTSUP remedy: the app always binds 0.0.0.0:5000 in code, so the real fixes are firewall/port config or a code change to honor HOST, not setting the env var. Keep MSSQL_PORT only if a non-1433 instance is documented as a known limitation.

findings.location: Running as a Windows Service > Option A: repeated 'nssm set ... AppEnvironmentExtra "..."' calls (one per line)
findings.docSays: Sets each environment variable with a separate 'nssm set ClientIQ-Dev AppEnvironmentExtra "..."' command (first NODE_ENV=development, then +PORT=5000, +HOST=..., etc.).
findings.actualState: NSSM AppEnvironmentExtra is a single multi-string value; each separate 'nssm set ... AppEnvironmentExtra' call overwrites the previous one, so only the last line survives. The repo's own deploy generates one Start-Server.ps1 that sets all env vars in one process (start-script.yml) rather than layering NSSM AppEnvironmentExtra calls.
findings.recommendedChange: Set AppEnvironmentExtra once with all NEWLINE-separated KEY=VALUE pairs in a single command, or (matching the real deploy) point the service at a generated Start-Server.ps1 that exports the env and launches tsx. Note the '+' prefix syntax is not how nssm merges across separate invocations.

findings.location: Step 4 .env DB block: MSSQL_ENCRYPT=true; batch/PS scripts also set MSSQL_ENCRYPT=true
findings.docSays: MSSQL_ENCRYPT=true (and MSSQL_TRUST_SERVER_CERTIFICATE=true) for the SQL Server connection.
findings.actualState: The repo Start scripts and the deploy template all set MSSQL_ENCRYPT=false (Start-Dev.ps1:18, start-script.yml). MSSQL_ENCRYPT is honored only by the session store (server/auth/session.ts:15); the main data pool hard-codes encrypt: true and derives trust solely from NODE_ENV==='development' (server/dbConnection.ts:28-29), ignoring both vars (env-vars.md §4).
findings.recommendedChange: Align the value with the repo default (MSSQL_ENCRYPT=false for dev/test) and add a note that MSSQL_ENCRYPT/MSSQL_TRUST_SERVER_CERTIFICATE affect only the session-store connection; the main pool always uses encrypt:true and trusts the cert only in development.

findings.location: Common Windows Issue: NODE_ENV Not Recognized > dev.bat and inline 'set NODE_ENV=development && npm run dev'
findings.docSays: Presents 'NODE_ENV is not recognized' as a Windows problem for npm run dev and suggests 'set NODE_ENV=development && npm run dev' as a workaround.
findings.actualState: package.json 'dev' script is literally 'NODE_ENV=development tsx server/index.ts' (package.json:7), which is Unix-style and DOES fail on Windows cmd/PowerShell. But the repo's actual Windows launch never uses npm run dev; Start-Dev.ps1/Start-Server.ps1 and the deploy template invoke 'npx tsx watch --clear-screen=false server/index.ts' directly after setting env (deployment.md §4.1). The suggested 'set X && npm run dev' still runs the broken inline-NODE_ENV script.
findings.recommendedChange: Point readers at the existing repo scripts (Start-Dev.ps1 / npx tsx watch server/index.ts) as the supported Windows launch rather than npm run dev. Note that 'set NODE_ENV=development && npm run dev' does not fix the underlying script, because the npm script itself prefixes NODE_ENV=... which cmd cannot parse.

findings.location: Complete Dev/Test Environment Setup (Steps 1-5) — no database schema/migration or seed step
findings.docSays: Goes straight from npm install and .env creation to running the server; never provisions or migrates the SQL Server database schema, and never seeds baseline/reference data.
findings.actualState: The repo defines a Drizzle schema (shared/schema.ts) and a schema-push script db:push = drizzle-kit push (package.json). There is a documented data-seed process (facts/data-seed.md) and RBAC/role seed data (facts/rbac.md) the app needs to function. Note db:push/drizzle.config.ts is the PG-abstraction path (requires DATABASE_URL); SQL Server schema/seed provisioning is a separate step operators must perform.
findings.recommendedChange: Add a step covering database provisioning: how the ClientIQ_Dev SQL Server schema is created/migrated and how baseline reference/RBAC data is seeded before first run. Clarify that db:push targets the Postgres abstraction and is not the SQL Server provisioning path.

findings.location: Step 4 .env DB block (no DB_VENDOR)
findings.docSays: Sets DATABASE_DIALECT=sqlserver but does not set DB_VENDOR.
findings.actualState: The repo Start scripts and deploy template also set DB_VENDOR=mssql (Start-Dev.ps1, start-script.yml). DB_VENDOR drives search-provider selection in server/adapters/search/SearchProviderFactory.ts:25; if unset it falls back to detecting from DATABASE_URL and ultimately defaults to PostgreSQL with a warning (env-vars.md row DB_VENDOR).
findings.recommendedChange: Add DB_VENDOR=sqlserver (the scripts use 'mssql') alongside DATABASE_DIALECT=sqlserver so the search provider resolves to the SQL Server implementation instead of falling back to the Postgres default.

findings.location: Nginx site config: 'location /health { proxy_pass http://clientiq_backend/api/health; }' and 'add_header X-XSS-Protection'
findings.docSays: Maps nginx /health to the backend /api/health, and adds an X-XSS-Protection header.
findings.actualState: The app's health route is /api/health (server/routes.ts:3133); the authGate/requestLogger allowlist an exact '/health' path (authGate.ts:16, requestLogger.ts:13) but that is not the JSON health route. Verification steps elsewhere correctly hit /api/health directly. X-XSS-Protection is a deprecated header. Relevant only if a proxy is used at all (see nginx finding).
findings.recommendedChange: If any proxy is documented, proxy the public health path to /api/health and note the app also has a lightweight allowlisted /health. Drop or de-emphasize X-XSS-Protection as deprecated. Keep the direct /api/health checks in Verification Steps.

findings.location: Option A note: 'runs the TypeScript source with hot reloading disabled (for stability)' using tsx (not tsx watch)
findings.docSays: Service Option A runs tsx server/index.ts with hot reloading disabled for stability.
findings.actualState: The real deploy/runtime uses tsx WATCH: 'npx tsx watch --clear-screen=false server/index.ts' in Start-Dev.ps1, Start-Server.ps1, and the generated start-script.yml (deployment.md §1.5, §4.1). The pipeline-deployed server runs in watch mode with NODE_ENV=development (which also selects Vite dev middleware and mock/dev auth).
findings.recommendedChange: Align with the actual command (tsx watch) or explicitly state dev/test intentionally deviates by disabling watch. Add a note that NODE_ENV=development in this mode enables Vite dev middleware and, unless SAML_ENABLED=true, the dev mock-auth path (req.employeeId=1).

findings.location: Prerequisites / dev.bat vs Troubleshooting 'npm run dev'
findings.docSays: dev.bat launches 'npx tsx watch --clear-screen=false server/index.ts' after setting env vars, while other sections describe 'npm run dev'.
findings.actualState: The dev.bat tsx-watch invocation is correct and matches the repo scripts, but it silently diverges from the 'npm run dev' framing used elsewhere in the same doc, mixing two launch methods.
findings.recommendedChange: Standardize on one launch method (the tsx watch invocation used by Start-Dev.ps1) and remove the conflicting 'npm run dev' framing to avoid confusion.

findings.location: Header (Last updated by Haroun Ahmady, Apr 14 2026) / Version History (1.0.0, December 2025) / Assumptions Made
findings.docSays: Ownership 'Haroun Ahmady', version 1.0.0 dated December 2025, and a list of environment assumptions (NSSM path, Node path, SQL auth, SAML disabled for testing).
findings.actualState: Ownership, version cadence, and the concrete test-environment values (test-clientiq.fmb.com DNS, cert filenames, SQL server hostname/creds, whether SAML is enabled in test) cannot be verified from the repo. The repo confirms SQL auth (not Windows auth) and NSSM/C:\ClientIQ conventions, but host/DNS/cert facts are governance/infra.
findings.recommendedChange: Have the doc owner confirm current ownership, bump the version to reflect the corrections above, and verify environment-specific values (DNS, cert names, SQL host, SAML enablement in test) against the actual test environment / ADO variable groups (VG-Test).

docPurpose: DBA-facing runbook for installing, securing, backing up, and maintaining the ClientIQ database on Microsoft SQL Server (creation, schema load, security, backups, index/stats maintenance, monitoring, connection config, DR).
summary: The guide is correct in its core premise — SQL Server is the production engine — and its generic SQL Server DBA mechanics (backups, index/stats maintenance, DMV monitoring, DR) are broadly reusable and not wrong. However, the ClientIQ-specific steps are substantially out of sync with the repo: the schema-load step points to a consolidated DDL script (database-scripts/v3/schema/sqlserver-schema-v3.sql) and a test-data script (sqlserver-test-data-v3.sql) that do not exist anywhere in the codebase; the expected table count (39) is wrong (there are 40 pgTable definitions); the documented connection string and env-var block contradict what the deploy scripts actually set (Encrypt/TrustServerCertificate are inverted, DB_VENDOR is missing/uses a value the code path doesn't); and the guide omits every ClientIQ-specific prerequisite script the app actually needs on SQL Server (sessions table, audit_event table, performance indexes, and the SAML/RBAC bootstrap scripts). No PostgreSQL/trigram/dual-database claims are present. Net: the SQL Server framing is right, but the ClientIQ setup procedure would not work as written.

findings.location: Step 2: Create Schema — Run Schema Script
findings.docSays: "The schema script is located at: database-scripts/v3/schema/sqlserver-schema-v3.sql" and instructs running it via sqlcmd to build all tables.
findings.actualState: No such file or directory exists. There is no database-scripts/ directory and no sqlserver-schema*.sql anywhere in the repo (find over all 27 .sql files returns only Insert Queries/*.sql and scripts/*.sql). The production SQL Server schema is NOT managed by a single consolidated DDL script; the Drizzle pgTable definitions in shared/schema.ts are the type source, and physical tables come from a mix of manual DDL plus the standalone scripts under scripts/ and Insert Queries/Schema Changes/.
findings.recommendedChange: Remove the reference to database-scripts/v3/schema/sqlserver-schema-v3.sql. Replace Step 2 with the real process: schema is materialized on SQL Server via manual/out-of-band DDL (shared/schema.ts is the pgTable source of truth for structure) plus the required scripts/*.sql (create_sessions_table.sql, create_audit_event_table.sql) and Insert Queries/Schema Changes/*.sql migrations. If a consolidated schema script is desired, it must be created; it does not exist today.

findings.location: Step 3: Import Test Data — sqlcmd -i "sqlserver-test-data-v3.sql"
findings.docSays: "Run test data script: sqlcmd -S YourServer -d ClientIQ -i \"sqlserver-test-data-v3.sql\"" to populate customer/account/household/financial_transaction/employee.
findings.actualState: No sqlserver-test-data-v3.sql exists in the repo. Test/preprod data is loaded two different ways, neither named this: (a) SQL Server ETL under Insert Queries/*.sql (real data from Jack Henry TheSpot/TheVault views into ClientIQPreProd.dbo.*, loaded in FK order), and (b) the faker/dev fixture generator scripts/seed.ts which targets the PostgreSQL/Drizzle abstraction, not production SQL Server. There is no npm seed script wired in package.json.
findings.recommendedChange: Replace the fictitious script with the real options: for SQL Server, document the Insert Queries/*.sql ETL run in FK-dependency order (Lookup Tables first: branch, note_category, transaction_categories; then customer/employee; then dependent tables). Note scripts/seed.ts is faker/dev only and hits the Postgres abstraction — do not use it against production SQL Server.

findings.location: Step 2: Verify Schema Creation — table count comment
findings.docSays: "-- Expected: 39" table count after schema creation.
findings.actualState: shared/schema.ts defines 40 pgTable tables (verified: grep -c pgTable = 40), including debit_card_limit_profile, debit_card, online_banking_user, online_banking_login_event, contact_history which the doc's own verification query later ignores. The expected count is 40, not 39 (and this only holds if all pgTable tables are physically created, which the missing schema script calls into question anyway).
findings.recommendedChange: Update the expected table count to 40 to match shared/schema.ts, or better, list the authoritative table set. Note that whether all 40 exist physically on SQL Server depends on the actual DDL applied, since there is no single schema script.

findings.location: Step 9: Connection Configuration — Connection String for Application
findings.docSays: Connection string uses "Encrypt=true; TrustServerCertificate=false;" for the application connection to SQL Server.
findings.actualState: The main data pool (server/dbConnection.ts:28-29) hard-codes encrypt: true but sets trustServerCertificate solely from NODE_ENV==='development'; the pool ignores MSSQL_ENCRYPT/MSSQL_TRUST_SERVER_CERTIFICATE entirely. All deploy/start scripts set MSSQL_ENCRYPT=false and MSSQL_TRUST_SERVER_CERTIFICATE=true (start-script.yml:26-27, Start-Dev.ps1:18-19, Start-Server.ps1:35-36) and run NODE_ENV=development, so in practice the deployed app trusts self-signed certs. Those two env vars are actually only honored by the session store (server/auth/session.ts:15-16), not the main pool.
findings.recommendedChange: Correct the connection guidance: document that the main pool hard-codes encrypt:true and derives trustServerCertificate from NODE_ENV (dev => trust-any-cert), while MSSQL_ENCRYPT / MSSQL_TRUST_SERVER_CERTIFICATE only affect the session-store connection. Flag that deployed environments run NODE_ENV=development and therefore trust self-signed certs — call out the security implication rather than implying Encrypt=true/TrustServerCertificate=false is enforced.

findings.location: Step 9: Connection Configuration — Environment Variables (DATABASE_DIALECT=sqlserver, MSSQL_* block)
findings.docSays: Env block lists DATABASE_DIALECT=sqlserver, MSSQL_SERVER/DATABASE/USER/PASSWORD, MSSQL_PORT=1433, MSSQL_ENCRYPT=true, MSSQL_TRUST_SERVER_CERTIFICATE=false; and omits DB_VENDOR.
findings.actualState: Two things are off: (1) MSSQL_PORT is a dead env var — no process.env.MSSQL_PORT is read anywhere in code; the mssql pool uses the default port (env-vars facts §2). (2) The search subsystem needs DB_VENDOR set separately (server/adapters/search/SearchProviderFactory.ts:25); DATABASE_DIALECT (dbConfig) and DB_VENDOR are two independent switches that both default to Postgres if unset. Deploy scripts set DB_VENDOR=mssql (start-script.yml:20). Also MSSQL_ENCRYPT/TRUST values are inverted vs what deploy actually uses (see prior finding).
findings.recommendedChange: Add DB_VENDOR (start scripts use 'mssql'; the code also accepts 'sqlserver') alongside DATABASE_DIALECT=sqlserver, and explain both must be set for SQL Server selection in their respective subsystems. Mark MSSQL_PORT as informational-only / not read by the app (the pool uses the default 1433). Reconcile MSSQL_ENCRYPT/MSSQL_TRUST_SERVER_CERTIFICATE with actual deploy values (false/true) and note they only affect the session store.

findings.location: Whole guide — missing ClientIQ prerequisite scripts
findings.docSays: The guide covers generic DBA setup but documents no ClientIQ-specific prerequisite objects beyond the (nonexistent) schema script.
findings.actualState: Several scripts under scripts/ are required for the app / role-gated features to run on SQL Server: create_sessions_table.sql (dbo.sessions for connect-mssql-v2, required when SAML_ENABLED=true), create_audit_event_table.sql (dbo.audit_event + 7 indexes; the pgTable is not applied to SQL Server), create_performance_indexes.sql (perf indexes on financial_transaction/account_ownership/account/customer), plus the SAML/RBAC bootstrap scripts (see next finding). The sessions DB user needs db_datareader/db_datawriter/db_ddladmin.
findings.recommendedChange: Add a 'Required application objects / prerequisite scripts' section covering scripts/create_sessions_table.sql (+ fix_sessions_table.sql), scripts/create_audit_event_table.sql, and scripts/create_performance_indexes.sql, with when/why each is needed and the db_datareader/db_datawriter/db_ddladmin requirement for the sessions store.

findings.location: Whole guide — missing SAML/RBAC SQL Server bootstrap
findings.docSays: No mention of the SAML SSO / RBAC bootstrap that a SQL Server environment requires for logins and role assignment to work.
findings.actualState: SQL Server environments require standalone idempotent scripts the ETL does not run: scripts/ensure_branch_manager_role.sql (default 'Branch Manager' role so SAML auto-provisioned users get a role), scripts/ensure_rbac_provenance_columns.sql (adds employee_role.assigned_by and history provenance columns; required before enforced AD-group role sync), and scripts/widen_employee_last_seen_saml_role.sql (widens employee.last_seen_saml_role to NVARCHAR(MAX); without it, full AD group lists overflow varchar(255) → SQL error 2628, aborting the employee upsert and leaving SSO users stuck on 'Awaiting Role Assignment'). AD-group→role mapping is app code keyed on role.role_name (server/auth/adGroupRoleMap.ts), so matching role rows must exist.
findings.recommendedChange: Add an 'RBAC / SAML SSO bootstrap (SQL Server)' section documenting ensure_branch_manager_role.sql, ensure_rbac_provenance_columns.sql, and widen_employee_last_seen_saml_role.sql, plus the requirement that role rows exist for every name adGroupRoleMap.ts can emit. This is essential DBA-facing setup that is currently entirely absent.

findings.location: Whole guide — missing out-of-band schema-change migrations
findings.docSays: No mention of the incremental schema-change scripts that must be applied for current app features.
findings.actualState: Insert Queries/Schema Changes/ contains idempotent migrations the app depends on: financial_transaction_add_account_number.sql + financial_transaction_backfill_account_number.sql (financial_transaction.account_id is now nullable; the ETL pivoted joins onto account_number, so backfill is required before app queries repoint) and note_add_cif_number.sql (denormalized Jack Henry CIF on note). These add columns/indexes not present in a bare schema.
findings.recommendedChange: Add a 'Schema-change migrations' subsection listing the Insert Queries/Schema Changes/*.sql files, their idempotency, and the ordering constraint (backfill account_number before repointing transaction queries). Note financial_transaction.account_id is intentionally nullable now.

findings.location: Overview / Prerequisites / Step 9 — deployment model context
findings.docSays: Implies a conventional production SQL-Server-backed app deployment (Encrypt=true, TrustServerCertificate=false, production posture) without describing how the app actually runs.
findings.actualState: The ADO pipeline deploys the app as a Windows Service in C:\ClientIQ, launched via 'npx tsx watch server/index.ts' with NODE_ENV=development (start-script.yml:16,48), serving both API and client on a single un-firewalled port 5000. Because NODE_ENV=development, the deployed runtime uses dev/mock behaviors and trust-any-cert DB TLS. Deploys come from Azure DevOps branches (develop/test/preprod/prod), NOT GitHub main.
findings.recommendedChange: Add a short 'How the app connects in each environment' note so DBAs understand the deployed app runs NODE_ENV=development against SQL Server with MSSQL_ENCRYPT=false/trust-any-cert, on port 5000, and that DB connection posture is dev-relaxed. This affects security expectations a DBA would otherwise assume from the Encrypt=true connection string.

findings.location: Step 4: Security Configuration — Read-Only Access role membership
findings.docSays: "CREATE ROLE app_clientiq_readonly; ALTER ROLE db_datareader ADD MEMBER app_clientiq_readonly; ALTER ROLE app_clientiq_readonly ADD MEMBER svc_clientiq_readonly;"
findings.actualState: This is generic example DDL, not repo-derived, and the nesting is backwards for the intent: adding app_clientiq_readonly as a member of db_datareader (rather than granting reads to the custom role directly) then nesting the login role is confusing and non-idiomatic. Not a repo fact, but a DBA following it verbatim gets a fragile role graph.
findings.recommendedChange: Simplify to add svc_clientiq_readonly directly to db_datareader, or grant SELECT on schema::dbo to app_clientiq_readonly and add the login to that role. Minor; flagged as example-quality, not a codebase mismatch.

findings.location: Step 4: Row-Level Security (Optional) — fn_securitypredicate
findings.docSays: RLS predicate joins employee_branch/branch and filters dbo.customer on branch_id via a SESSION_CONTEXT employee_id, presented as a ClientIQ-applicable example.
findings.actualState: customer.branch_id does exist (shared/schema.ts:139) and employee_branch exists, so the shape is plausible, but the app does not use SQL Server RLS or SESSION_CONTEXT — authorization is enforced in app code (RBAC + ABAC in server/, adGroupRoleMap, permission checks). The predicate function's inner logic also conflates @region_id with branch_id. This is illustrative only and not wired to the running app.
findings.recommendedChange: Keep as clearly-labeled optional/illustrative, but state explicitly that ClientIQ enforces access control in application code (RBAC/ABAC), not via SQL Server RLS, so this is not part of the standard setup.

findings.location: Support Contacts / Maintenance Checklist / file placement (D:/E:/F: drives)
findings.docSays: Support-contact SLAs (DBA on-call 15 min, etc.), maintenance cadence, and specific file paths (D:\SQLData, E:\SQLLogs, F:\SQLBackups).
findings.actualState: None of these (ownership, SLAs, storage layout, backup schedule) are derivable from the repo; they are governance/infra decisions. Cannot confirm or refute from code.
findings.recommendedChange: Have the DBA/ops owner confirm the on-call contacts, SLAs, drive layout, and backup cadence for the actual on-prem SQL Server hosts; mark these sections as environment-specific and verify against the real server build.

docPurpose: Product/architecture overview wiki for the ClientIQ (Banking Client 360) customer-360 CRM: describes core features, search, data model, tech stack, design system, test data, and differentiators.
summary: The feature narrative (search, profiles, accounts, transactions, notes, RBAC surfaces, household mapping) is broadly accurate and still describes the app well. The document is badly outdated on infrastructure and data facts: it repeatedly frames the system as a live "dual-database PostgreSQL + SQL Server" platform with trigram fuzzy search, when production is SQL Server only, search is a case-insensitive LIKE substring match, and the Postgres/Drizzle-pg layer is a non-runtime abstraction. Several concrete numbers and claims are wrong (test-data counts of 505 vs seed's 1200, primary brand color #2e7d32 vs actual #1b4d20, "automatic PostgreSQL triggers," and a "CI/CD Governance" section with pre-commit hooks / npm audit that does not exist in the repo). The doc also omits the SAML/AD-group RBAC system that is central to the current app. Both source files (docs/WIKI.md and the extracted ClientIQ_-_Overview.txt) are essentially identical and share every finding below.

findings.docSays: Fuzzy matching: Handles typos and spelling variations using PostgreSQL trigram similarity or SQL Server phonetic matching. Example: Fuzzy name 'Smyth' finds 'Smith' with 33% similarity.
findings.actualState: Production search is SQL Server case-insensitive substring matching: 'c.first_name COLLATE Latin1_General_CI_AS LIKE @searchPattern' (etc.) across first/last/business/full name, tax_identifier, silverlake_customer_id, and CONCAT(first,last), in server/storage/sqlServerCustomerSearch.ts:103-126. There is no pg_trgm/trigram similarity and no phonetic (SOUNDEX/DIFFERENCE) matching in the SQL Server path; it is exact substring LIKE. The Postgres trigram provider (server/adapters/search/PostgresSearchProvider.ts) exists only in the non-production abstraction.
findings.location: Core Features > 1. Customer Search & Discovery > Intelligent Hybrid Search; Search Examples
findings.recommendedChange: Replace the trigram/phonetic 'fuzzy matching' claim with the real behavior: case-insensitive substring (LIKE with Latin1_General_CI_AS collation) across name/business/full_name/tax id/silverlake id/concatenated name on SQL Server. Remove the 'Smyth finds Smith with 33% similarity' example (substring LIKE would not match that) or replace with a valid substring example. Drop 'phonetic matching' unless/until it is actually implemented.

findings.docSays: Dual-database support: Seamlessly works with both PostgreSQL and Microsoft SQL Server backends. Database: Dual support for PostgreSQL and Microsoft SQL Server. Key Differentiator #5: Dual-Database Architecture: Seamlessly switch between PostgreSQL and SQL Server.
findings.actualState: SQL Server is the only production engine. server/dbConnection.ts is titled 'MS SQL Server only (on-prem deployment)'; getDatabase() returns an mssql pool with db:null (dbConnection.ts:49-52), and the PG helpers are stubs where getPgDatabase() throws 'not available - this deployment uses MS SQL only' (dbConnection.ts:74-79). The pgTable schema, drizzle.config (dialect=postgresql), and the default-Postgres branches of dbConfig/SearchProviderFactory are a residual abstraction, not a live second backend. There is no runtime path that connects to PostgreSQL.
findings.location: Core Features > 1; Technical Capabilities > Architecture; Technical Capabilities > Dual-Database Support; Key Differentiators #5
findings.recommendedChange: Reframe 'dual-database' as an internal abstraction, not a supported runtime capability: state SQL Server (MSSQL_* env vars) is the sole production engine; the SearchProvider/adapter pattern and pgTable schema are a portability abstraction with a non-runtime Postgres path. Delete or heavily qualify the 'Dual-Database Support' section and Key Differentiator #5 so readers do not believe they can run on Postgres.

findings.docSays: Automatic triggers: PostgreSQL triggers maintain computed fields. Index optimization: Trigram GIN indexes and Full-Text Search support.
findings.actualState: No PostgreSQL triggers or GIN/trigram indexes run in production (SQL Server only). shared/schema.ts (pgTable) declares only plain btree-style indexes (e.g. idx_customer_full_name at schema.ts:155-163), no GIN/trigram. Physical SQL Server indexes are created via scripts/create_performance_indexes.sql (nonclustered INCLUDE indexes), not GIN. Debit-card business rules are enforced by SQL Server DB triggers per the schema.ts:430-450 comment, not Postgres triggers; full_name is described as a generated column (schema.ts:114-115), not maintained by a PG trigger at runtime.
findings.location: Technical Capabilities > Data Quality & Integrity
findings.recommendedChange: Remove 'PostgreSQL triggers' and 'Trigram GIN indexes and Full-Text Search'. Replace with the SQL Server reality: SQL Server computed/persisted columns, nonclustered performance indexes (scripts/create_performance_indexes.sql), and SQL Server triggers for debit-card rules. findings.docSays: Test Data: 505 total customers (175 individual, 159 business, 171 trust). Extensive transaction history across 90+ days.

docPurpose: Operator-facing overview and index for deploying ClientIQ / Banking Client 360 on-premises to Windows Server + SQL Server, covering architecture, a documentation index, deployment checklist/steps, system requirements, network ports, and support contacts.
summary: The doc is broadly correct on the big-picture stack (Windows Server host, SQL Server backend, SAML/RSA auth, single Node app port 5000, PowerShell/Windows-service deploy) but is materially wrong or silent on how the app is actually run and fronted. Its most consequential gaps: (1) it presents Nginx as the reverse proxy/TLS terminator, yet there is no Nginx anywhere in the repo and the actual deploy pipeline is Azure DevOps → PowerShell Remoting → Windows Service running the app from TypeScript source via tsx watch with NODE_ENV=development (not a compiled production build); (2) it omits the entire ADO/branch-based deploy model (deploy from ADO branches, not GitHub main; DAST scan; per-env SAML role scoping); and (3) it misnames the RSA IdP and omits key operational realities (dev-mode runtime, single port bound to 0.0.0.0, session-table DDL prerequisite, out-of-band SQL Server schema scripts). No hard PostgreSQL claims appear in this overview doc, but the doc's silence on the ADO pipeline and the dev-mode runtime are the headline problems for anyone actually deploying.

findings.docSays: The deployment architecture uses Nginx as the reverse proxy with SSL termination, drawn as "Nginx (Port 443) SSL Termination" fronting the Node.js app; Document 02 is "02-NGINX-REVERSE-PROXY.md".
findings.actualState: There is no Nginx config, reference, or service anywhere in the repo (recursive grep for 'nginx' across *.yml/*.md/*.ts/*.conf returns nothing; confirmed in deployment.md §5.2). The Node app listens on plain HTTP and does not terminate TLS itself. SAML URLs are all https:// (PipelineTemplates/start-script.yml:32-36), so some external TLS terminator is expected, but nothing in this repo configures Nginx specifically. The only in-repo reverse proxy is the app-level Express Streamlit proxy at /streamlit (server/proxy.ts), which proxies OUT to Streamlit, not in front of the app.
findings.recommendedChange: Stop asserting Nginx as the reverse proxy. Reword to: "An external TLS terminator / reverse proxy (product not defined in this repo) fronts the Node app, which itself listens on plain HTTP port 5000." Either remove the '02-NGINX-REVERSE-PROXY.md' index entry or reframe it as generic reverse-proxy guidance and flag that no proxy config ships with the application.

findings.location: Deployment Steps / Overview — 'Application Deployment' step ("Extract application package … Start application service")
findings.docSays: Application deployment is a generic manual sequence: extract application package, configure environment variables, start application service, verify health endpoints. No CI/CD pipeline, branch model, or artifact source is described.
findings.actualState: Deployment is driven by an Azure DevOps pipeline (azure-pipelines.yml + PipelineTemplates/). Preprod/prod deploy from ADO branches (develop/test/preprod/prod), NOT GitHub main — pushing to GitHub main does not reach preprod/prod (deployment.md §1, project ops rule). The pipeline builds on an ADO agent, publishes an artifact (node_modules excluded), then via PowerShell Remoting copies the artifact to C:\ClientIQ, stops the Windows service, optionally runs 'npm ci' (only when the commit message contains 'npm ci'), and restarts the service (PipelineTemplates/deploy-nodejs.yml). Branch→env→SAMLRoleEnv: develop→Dev(DEV), test→Test(TST)+DAST, preprod→PreProd(STG), prod→Prod(PRD) on two servers (Deploy_Prod + Deploy_Prod2).
findings.recommendedChange: Add an 'Azure DevOps deployment pipeline' section documenting the branch→environment mapping, that deploys originate from ADO branches (not GitHub main), the PowerShell-Remoting copy→stop-service→(optional npm ci)→start-service flow, the 'npm ci' commit-message gate, and that prod deploys to two servers. findings.location: Overview / Deployment Steps — implied production run of the Node.js application
findings.docSays: The guide frames a production deployment of "the Node.js application" on Windows Server (Documentation Index row 01 says "Windows Server and Node.js configuration (Production)").
findings.actualState: The pipeline-generated start script sets NODE_ENV="development" for every environment and launches the app via 'npx tsx watch --clear-screen=false server/index.ts' (PipelineTemplates/start-script.yml:15,48 — verified). It runs from TypeScript source in watch mode, NOT the compiled dist/index.js, and NOT with NODE_ENV=production. Consequences (server/index.ts): the app serves the client through Vite dev middleware (setupVite) rather than static dist/public, session cookies are non-secure, the main SQL pool trusts self-signed certs, dev-only debug routes activate, and — unless SAML_ENABLED=true — the dev mock-auth branch injects employeeId=1 (Sarah Johnson, System Admin). package.json 'start' (NODE_ENV=production node dist/index.js) is NOT what the pipeline runs.
findings.recommendedChange: Call out explicitly that the deployed runtime currently runs 'tsx watch' from source with NODE_ENV=development on all environments (a real dev/prod configuration mismatch), and document the security/behavioral consequences (Vite dev middleware, non-secure cookies, mock auth when SAML is off). Recommend operators confirm whether the Windows service env overrides NODE_ENV to production, and align the doc with whatever is actually intended.

findings.location: Overview + Architecture Diagram — "SAML 2.0 - Enterprise authentication via RSA Identity Provider" / IdP box "RSA Authentication Mgr"
findings.docSays: SAML 2.0 authentication is provided by the "RSA Identity Provider", drawn in the diagram as "RSA Authentication Mgr".
findings.actualState: The IdP is RSA SecurID Access (the F&M Bank RSA portal), not RSA Authentication Manager (saml-ad.md §1; server/routes/auth.ts:107 renders "Sign in via the F&M Bank RSA portal"). The strategy is deliberately configured for RSA SecurID Access: it signs the SAML Response wrapper (not the Assertion), so both wantAssertionsSigned and wantAuthnResponseSigned are false (server/auth/samlStrategy.ts:135-139). The IdP host is portal.fmb.com and SSO is launched from the ClientIQ portal tile (RSA only emits a SAMLResponse when launched from the tile; direct IdPServlet links do not initiate SSO — server/routes/auth.ts:138-142).
findings.recommendedChange: Correct the IdP name to 'RSA SecurID Access (F&M Bank RSA portal)'. Note the portal.fmb.com host, the tile-launch requirement, and the Response-wrapper (not Assertion) signature model that drives the wantAssertionsSigned/wantAuthnResponseSigned=false configuration.

findings.location: Deployment Steps — 5. Database Setup ("Create database and schema … Import reference data")
findings.docSays: Database setup is: create database and schema, import reference data, configure security, set up backups. No mention of how the SQL Server schema is actually created or of required out-of-band scripts.
findings.actualState: Production SQL Server schema is NOT managed by drizzle-kit (drizzle.config.ts targets PostgreSQL and throws without DATABASE_URL). It is created by standalone idempotent SQL Server scripts under scripts/ and 'Insert Queries/Schema Changes/' (db-schema.md §11). Deployment-critical prerequisites include: scripts/create_sessions_table.sql (dbo.sessions for connect-mssql-v2, REQUIRED when SAML_ENABLED=true — session login fails without it), scripts/ensure_branch_manager_role.sql (default SAML role), scripts/ensure_rbac_provenance_columns.sql (employee_role.assigned_by, needed for AD-group role sync), scripts/widen_employee_last_seen_saml_role.sql (NVARCHAR(MAX) to avoid SQL error 2628 stranding SSO users), scripts/create_audit_event_table.sql, scripts/create_performance_indexes.sql, and the financial_transaction/note denormalization scripts.
findings.recommendedChange: Add a 'SQL Server schema provisioning' subsection listing the required scripts in run order and stating that drizzle-kit/db:push is NOT the production schema mechanism (it targets PostgreSQL). Explicitly flag scripts/create_sessions_table.sql as a hard prerequisite for SAML login and the widen/ensure scripts as prerequisites for RBAC/SAML role sync.

findings.location: Overview / Documentation Index / SAML Configuration step
findings.docSays: SAML setup is described only as 'exchange metadata, configure attribute mapping, set up role synchronization, test SSO flow', with no detail on how roles are derived or environment scoping.
findings.actualState: Role assignment on login is convention-based from AD group names in the SAML 'role' attribute (server/auth/adGroupRoleMap.ts), keyed to the pattern <PREFIX>_<ENV>_APP_ClientIQ_<RoleToken>_<Access>. The SAML_ROLE_ENV env var (DEV/TST/STG/PRD) scopes which environment's AD groups are honored — set per ADO stage (develop→DEV, test→TST, preprod→STG, prod→PRD; azure-pipelines.yml). Because one on-prem AD carries every env's groups, SAML_ROLE_ENV is required to avoid cross-env role bleed. The saml_role_mapping DB table is admin-CRUD only and DORMANT — it does NOT drive login role assignment (saml-ad.md §7). A 'Branch Manager' default-role safety net prevents users from being stranded on 'Awaiting Role Assignment'.
findings.recommendedChange: Add SAML role-mapping detail: the AD-group naming convention, the required per-environment SAML_ROLE_ENV scoping, the SAML_DEFAULT_ROLE_NAME/'Branch Manager' fallback, and an explicit note that the saml_role_mapping table is not on the login path. Tie SAML_ROLE_ENV to the branch/environment table.

findings.location: System Requirements — Documentation Index / no environment-variable reference in the Overview

SAML_ENTITY_ID also has a stray trailing ')' in its literal value (start-script.yml:32). Additionally MSSQL_ENCRYPT/MSSQL_TRUST_SERVER_CERTIFICATE are honored ONLY by the session store; the main data pool hardcodes encrypt:true and derives trust solely from NODE_ENV==='development' (server/dbConnection.ts:28-29 — verified), so the deploy's MSSQL_ENCRYPT=false affects only the session connection.

docPurpose: Instructs the Data team which tables to populate (in FK order, with copy-paste SQL) so RBAC-gated and relationship features work in a BankClient360/ClientIQ test environment.
summary: The document's RBAC core (privilege_level, role, permission, role_permission, employee_role — Steps 1-5) is accurate against scripts/seed.ts and shared/schema.ts: the 5 levels, 9 roles, 11 permissions, min_privilege_level values, and the two-tier grant model all match. Its main weakness is that it presents one generic 32-step "load everything" recipe without acknowledging that BankClient360 has TWO disjoint data-load worlds — the faker/dev seed (scripts/seed.ts, the PG abstraction) and the real SQL Server ETL (Insert Queries/*.sql targeting ClientIQPreProd) — and that many tables in its load order (region, sic_code family, debit_card_limit_profile, entity_contact, note/note_version, online_banking_*, employee_branch) have NO SQL Server ETL loader at all. It also omits that RBAC must be bootstrapped separately on SQL Server (the ETL never touches RBAC; ensure_branch_manager_role.sql / ensure_rbac_provenance_columns.sql / widen_employee_last_seen_saml_role.sql), misstates the debit_card model for SQL Server (inline limit columns, not a debit_card_limit_profile FK), and frames the "employee customer protection" scenario in a way that overstates what the code enforces and provides no is_employee data. No hard PostgreSQL/trigram/dual-database claims appear in the doc text itself, but the doc silently assumes a single generic SQL dialect while the codebase is explicitly SQL-Server-only with a residual PG abstraction.

findings.docSays: Presents a single generic set of INSERT statements and one 32-step 'Complete Table Load Order' as if there is one way to groom the data.
findings.actualState: There are two disjoint data-load paths that must not be conflated: (1) the faker/dev seed scripts/seed.ts (targets the PostgreSQL/Drizzle-pg abstraction; uses pg_get_serial_sequence/setval, is_active=true) generating synthetic data (faker.seed(12345), scripts/seed.ts:12; main() self-invokes at scripts/seed.ts:833); and (2) the real SQL Server ETL in 'Insert Queries/*.sql' targeting ClientIQPreProd.dbo.* from Jack Henry views (TheSpot/TheSpotPreProd/TheVault). A preprod/SQL Server test env is groomed by the .sql ETL, not the seed. The doc never names either mechanism, scripts/seed.ts, or the Insert Queries/ folder.
findings.location: Whole document / Summary / Quick Reference: Complete Table Load Order
findings.recommendedChange: Add an up-front section distinguishing the faker dev seed (scripts/seed.ts) from the SQL Server ETL (Insert Queries/*.sql -> ClientIQPreProd). State which one a SQL Server preprod env actually uses, and point the reader at the real ETL files instead of hand-written generic INSERTs.

findings.docSays: Lists region, sic_code, customer_sic_code, account_sic_code, debit_card_limit_profile, entity_contact, note, note_version, online_banking_user, online_banking_login_event, and employee_branch in the 32-step load order as if each is loadable, and puts region in Priority 1 with SQL implied.
findings.actualState: None of these tables has a SQL Server ETL loader in Insert Queries/. Verified: no INSERT/MERGE into dbo.region, dbo.sic_code, dbo.customer_sic_code, dbo.account_sic_code, dbo.debit_card_limit_profile, dbo.entity_contact, dbo.note, dbo.note_version, dbo.online_banking_user, dbo.online_banking_login_event, or dbo.employee_branch exists (ls of 'Insert Queries/', 'Insert Queries/Lookup Tables/', 'Insert Queries/Schema Changes/'). branch.sql inserts only branch_code/branch_name/address_id and never populates region_id or a region table (Insert Queries/Lookup Tables/branch.sql:91-93). employee_branch exists in schema (shared/schema.ts:288) but is loaded by neither the seed nor the ETL.
findings.location: Priority 1 (region), Priority 2 (sic_code family, debit_card_limit_profile), Priority 3 (note_version, online_banking_*), Quick Reference load order steps 2, 11, 14, 19-21, 23, 30-32
findings.recommendedChange: Mark each table that has no SQL Server ETL loader as 'no ETL — must be hand-loaded / not populated in preprod', or drop them from the SQL Server load order. Only note_category, contact_history, customer_officer_assignment, household, household_membership, account_ownership, account, customer, employee, address, contact_info, entity_address, debit_card, financial_transaction, branch, and transaction_category have loaders.

findings.docSays: Priority 0 RBAC is presented as ordinary table loads with no note about how RBAC is bootstrapped on the production engine.
findings.actualState: On SQL Server the ETL (Insert Queries/*.sql) never touches RBAC tables, so RBAC must be bootstrapped by standalone idempotent scripts: scripts/ensure_branch_manager_role.sql (guarantees the Branch Manager fallback role used by SAML auto-provisioning), scripts/ensure_rbac_provenance_columns.sql (adds employee_role.assigned_by; required before enforced AD-group role sync works), and scripts/widen_employee_last_seen_saml_role.sql (widens employee.last_seen_saml_role to NVARCHAR(MAX) to avoid SQL error 2628 truncation that strands SSO users). None of these are mentioned.
findings.location: Priority 0 — RBAC Tables (BLOCKER)
findings.recommendedChange: Add a note that on SQL Server the ETL does not load RBAC, and reference the three scripts/*.sql bootstrap scripts. Note that in production, roles/role assignments are normally driven by SAML/AD-group sync, not by hand-inserted employee_role rows.

findings.docSays: Priority 2 table lists debit_card_limit_profile ('Card spending limits', profile_id/profile_name/daily_purchase_limit) and says debit_card depends on debit_card_limit_profile; the load order loads debit_card_limit_profile (step 23) before debit_card (step 24).
findings.actualState: The SQL Server debit_card ETL carries INLINE limit columns (daily_withdrawal_limit, daily_purchase_limit, daily_transaction_limit) sourced from TheSpotPreProd.dbo.DBT_CRD_VIEW and has NO limit_profile_id FK (Insert Queries/debit_card.sql:7-9). The debit_card_limit_profile / FK model exists only in the faker seed path (scripts/seed.ts). So on SQL Server there is no debit_card_limit_profile dependency and no such table is loaded.
findings.location: Priority 2 — Feature Enhancement Tables (debit_card / debit_card_limit_profile rows); Quick Reference steps 23-24
findings.recommendedChange: For the SQL Server path, remove debit_card_limit_profile as a dependency of debit_card and describe debit_card's inline limit columns. Only keep the limit-profile model if documenting the dev/faker seed, and label it as such.

findings.docSays: Test Scenarios: 'Employee customer protection — A customer with is_employee = 1 + a Level 1 user (should be blocked) + a Level 3 user (should see data)', implying general record access is gated by level.
findings.actualState: The is_employee restriction is a single ABAC rule attached ONLY to the transaction.view permission (scripts/seed.ts:136-145: customer.isEmployee equals true, denyIfMatch, minPrivilegeOverride:3), i.e. it gates viewing a bank-employee customer's TRANSACTIONS, not all their data. It is evaluated by the PG permissionService; in SQL Server mode permissionService.checkPermission returns {allowed:true} when db is null and the SQL Server store's checkPermission implements only branch/region conditions, so this employee-record control may not actually fire in production (see rbac facts §11.3). Additionally, no is_employee=1 data is produced: generatePersons() never sets isEmployee (scripts/seed.ts:251-291) and customer.sql has no is_employee mapping — testers must set is_employee manually.
findings.location: Test Scenarios Enabled by Data (Employee customer protection row)
findings.recommendedChange: Reword to say the restriction applies specifically to transaction.view (transaction history of employee-customers requires privilege >= 3), warn that SQL Server enforcement of this ABAC rule is unverified/likely gapped, and note that neither loader sets is_employee=1 so the tester must set it by hand to exercise this scenario.

findings.docSays: Step 3 permission table describes is_attribute_based (1 = has ABAC conditions) and marks transaction.view as attribute-based, but supplies no attributeConfig/conditions payload.
findings.actualState: transaction.view is the only attribute-based permission and its meaning comes entirely from its attributeConfig JSON (conditions: [{attribute:'customer.isEmployee', operator:'equals', value:true, denyIfMatch:true, minPrivilegeOverride:3, reason:'Employee customer records require Level 3+ access'}], scripts/seed.ts:136-145). Setting is_attribute_based=1 without inserting the conditions payload produces a permission whose ABAC rule is empty/undefined. The doc's INSERT provides no conditions column value.
findings.location: Priority 0 — Step 3: permission (transaction.view row)
findings.recommendedChange: Document the attributeConfig/conditions payload for transaction.view and note that the SQL Server store reads a 'conditions' column (branch/region model) rather than attribute_config (see schema vs SQL Server divergence), so the exact column and JSON shape depend on which engine's DDL is in the target DB.

findings.docSays: Priority 2 transaction_category key columns listed as 'category_id, name, group_code'.
findings.actualState: The SQL Server ETL inserts category_code, group_code, name into dbo.transaction_category (Insert Queries/Lookup Tables/transaction_categories.sql), and category_code is the actual join key to financial_transaction (LEFT JOIN transaction_category tc ON tc.category_code = s.TRANSACTION_CD, Insert Queries/financial_transaction.sql:40-41). category_code is omitted from the doc's key-columns list even though it is the load/join key. (Note: category_code is not in shared/schema.ts's transactionCategory definition (schema.ts:370) — it is a SQL-Server-only column, another schema-vs-SQL-Server divergence.)
findings.location: Priority 2 — Feature Enhancement Tables (transaction_category row)
findings.recommendedChange: Add category_code to the transaction_category key columns and note that financial_transaction joins on transaction_category.category_code (SQL Server), not category_id.

findings.docSays: Notes tables (note_category, note, note_version) are listed as Priority 3 to enable notes features; no mention of RBAC gating on notes.
findings.actualState: There is NO notes.* permission anywhere in schema, seed, or DB, and the entire notes surface (GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/notes*, note-categories) is authentication-only, not permission-gated; the Notes UI renders with no PermissionGuard (client/src/components/CustomerDashboard.tsx:863-869). So notes are readable/writable by any authenticated employee regardless of role. Also, note/note_version have no SQL Server ETL loader (only note_category does).
findings.location: Priority 3 — Notes & Audit Tables; Test Scenarios
findings.recommendedChange: Note that notes require no RBAC permission (auth-only) and that note/note_version have no ETL loader; only note_category is loaded by Insert Queries/Lookup Tables/note_category.sql.

findings.docSays: Load order step 26 financial_transaction with no note on time-boxing or on the account_number schema-change dependency.
findings.actualState: financial_transaction.sql only loads the last 13 months (WHERE TRANSACTION_DT >= DATEADD(MONTH,-13,GETDATE()), Insert Queries/financial_transaction.sql:42) — date-range tests older than 13 months see no data. Separately, Insert Queries/Schema Changes/financial_transaction_add_account_number.sql + _backfill_account_number.sql add/backfill a denormalized account_number column that the app's transaction queries repoint onto (ETL no longer reliably populates account_id) — these Schema Changes are prerequisites the doc omits entirely.
findings.location: Priority 2 (financial_transaction) / Quick Reference step 26
findings.recommendedChange: Add that transaction data is time-boxed to 13 months, and reference the Insert Queries/Schema Changes/*.sql migrations (add/backfill account_number, note cif_number) that must run for transaction/notes queries to work.

findings.docSays: Priority 1 region row and load-order step 2 imply region_id links branch to a populated region table (branch_id, branch_code, branch_name, region_id; region_id -> region).
findings.actualState: branch.region_id is a real FK in shared/schema.ts:288-ish (regionId references region.regionId), but the SQL Server branch.sql populates only branch_code/branch_name/address_id and never sets region_id (Insert Queries/Lookup Tables/branch.sql:91-93); no ETL loads region. In the faker seed, 'region' is just a string field on branch (scripts/seed.ts:39), not the region table. So region_id is effectively unpopulated in both paths.
findings.location: Priority 1 — Core Relationship Tables (region/branch); Quick Reference step 2-3
findings.recommendedChange: State that region is not loaded by any ETL and branch.region_id is left NULL in preprod; if regions are needed, they must be hand-loaded. Do not present region as a routine step 2.

docPurpose: Operational registry of the Active Directory security groups that grant access to the ClientIQ (Banking Client 360) application, listing each pre-prod group name, its purpose, data classification, and business owner.
summary: The document is a bare listing of 9 pre-prod (STG) AD security groups with owner and data-classification metadata. The group names themselves are largely accurate and match what the code's convention-based mapper expects, so it is not badly wrong — but it is substantially incomplete. It never explains how any group maps to an application role, omits the naming convention, the SAML_ROLE_ENV environment-scoping behavior, the meaning of the access suffixes and the GEN entitlement, and it omits the production (PRD) group set entirely. There is also a naming inconsistency around the admin group (the doc lists AppAdmin/STG while the code comments describe APPSVCS/PRE for preprod), and the doc obscures that DataAnalyst and BusinessBanker do not get their own app roles.

findings.location: Whole document (group list has no role-mapping column)
findings.docSays: Lists group names with a prose description and 'Owner'/'Data Classification', e.g. 'CTRL_STG_APP_ClientIQ_Teller_RO — Read-only Access ... for Tellers'. It never states which ClientIQ application role each group grants.

The RoleToken is captured by CLIENTIQ_GROUP_RE (adGroupRoleMap.ts:64).
