findings.location: Whole document — no naming-convention or env-scoping explanation
findings.docSays: No explanation of the group name structure, the ENV segment, the access suffix, or how one on-prem AD serves multiple deployment environments.
findings.actualState: Group naming convention is <PREFIX>_<ENV>_APP_ClientIQ_<RoleToken>_<Access> (adGroupRoleMap.ts:5-15). The ENV segment (DEV/TST/STG/PRD) and access suffix (RO/RW/MOD/ADM/EXEC) are ignored for role selection — only the RoleToken matters (adGroupRoleMap.ts:12-15). Because one on-prem AD carries every environment's groups, SAML_ROLE_ENV scopes which env's groups are honored per deployment (adGroupRoleMap.ts:116-162; normalizeRoleEnv adGroupRoleMap.ts:78-86). Preprod deploys with SAML_ROLE_ENV=STG (env-vars facts: azure-pipelines.yml:181-182).
findings.recommendedChange: Add a section explaining the naming convention, that the access suffix does not affect the granted role, and that SAML_ROLE_ENV (STG for preprod, PRD for prod) restricts which environment's groups are honored so the same AD user resolves to different roles per deployment.

findings.location: Production group set (document lists only CTRL_STG_* / IAM_STG_* pre-prod groups)
findings.docSays: Header 'Client IQ Pre-Prod Groups' followed only by STG-segment groups (CTRL_STG_APP_ClientIQ_*, IAM_STG_APP_RSA_ClientIQ_GEN_EXEC). No production (PRD) groups are listed.
findings.actualState: Production is a distinct deployment that runs with SAML_ROLE_ENV=PRD and therefore honors only PRD-segment groups (e.g. CTRL_PRD_APP_ClientIQ_BranchManager_MOD per adGroupRoleMap.ts:7). deployment facts: prod stage maps to PRD (deployment.md:240). The equivalent CTRL_PRD_* / IAM_PRD_* production groups are not documented here.
findings.recommendedChange: Either add a parallel 'Production Groups' section listing the CTRL_PRD_* / IAM_PRD_* groups, or state explicitly that this page covers pre-prod only and link to the production group registry.

findings.location: CTRL_STG_APP_ClientIQ_AppAdmin_ADM (admin group entry)
findings.docSays: Names the pre-prod administrative group 'CTRL_STG_APP_ClientIQ_AppAdmin_ADM' (STG segment, AppAdmin token).
findings.actualState: The code's authoritative comment states the admin group token differs by environment: APPSVCS in preprod with the form CTRL_PRE_..._APPSVCS_ADM, and AppAdmin in dev/test/stg/prod (adGroupRoleMap.ts:27-39). Both appsvcs and appadmin tokens are mapped to System Admin (adGroupRoleMap.ts:43-44). The doc's preprod admin group name (STG + AppAdmin) does not match the APPSVCS/PRE preprod form the code documents.
findings.recommendedChange: Reconcile the preprod admin group name with the entitlement source of truth: confirm whether preprod uses APPSVCS (CTRL_PRE_..._APPSVCS_ADM) or AppAdmin (CTRL_STG_..._AppAdmin_ADM), and document both tokens since the mapper accepts either. Note both resolve to the System Admin role (privilege 4).

findings.location: CTRL_STG_APP_ClientIQ_DataAnalyst_RO
findings.docSays: 'Read-only Access to ClientIQ application for Data Analysts' — implies Data Analysts are a distinct access/role group.
findings.actualState: The dataanalyst token maps to the Teller role (privilege 1), not a distinct Data Analyst role (adGroupRoleMap.ts:57). There is no 'Data Analyst' role in the role table; members of this group receive Teller-level permissions.
findings.recommendedChange: Clarify that members of the DataAnalyst group are granted the Teller application role (privilege 1), i.e. Data Analyst is an AD grouping that maps onto Teller permissions, not a separate application role.

findings.location: CTRL_STG_APP_ClientIQ_BusinessBanker_RW
findings.docSays: 'Read and Write Access ... for Banking Relationship Specialists and Lending Specialists'.
findings.actualState: The businessbanker token maps to the app role 'BRS' (Business Relationship Specialist, privilege 2) (adGroupRoleMap.ts:48). Note: 'BRS' is referenced by the mapper but is NOT created by scripts/seed.ts (which seeds separate 'Assistant Manager' and 'Business Banker' roles) and no in-repo migration creates it (rbac facts §3.3, adGroupRoleMap.ts:22-24). If the BRS role row is absent in SQL Server, sync falls back to the default role.
findings.recommendedChange: State that this group resolves to the 'BRS' application role (privilege 2) and note the dependency that a role row named exactly 'BRS' must exist in the SQL Server role table (it is not created by the seed script), otherwise affected users fall back to the default role.

findings.location: IAM_STG_APP_RSA_ClientIQ_GEN_EXEC
findings.docSays: 'Staging IAM Application RSA ClientIQ Execute' — no explanation of what access this grants inside ClientIQ.
findings.actualState: The GEN token is an access-only entitlement that maps to NO application role (ACCESS_ONLY_TOKENS = {'gen'}, adGroupRoleMap.ts:60-61; skipped at adGroupRoleMap.ts:152-153). A user holding only GEN/RSA access is authenticated but has no AD-derived role, so they fall back to the default role SAML_DEFAULT_ROLE_NAME (default 'Branch Manager') via the sync/bulletproof fallback (adGroupRoleMap.ts:14-15; auth.ts:357,412-424).
findings.recommendedChange: Explain that the IAM RSA GEN group is the 'may access the app' entitlement only — it grants no role by itself, and a user with only GEN receives the configured default role (Branch Manager) rather than being blocked.

findings.location: Whole document — default-role / unmatched behavior not stated
findings.docSays: No mention of what happens when a user's groups map to no role, or how the app guarantees an authenticated user is not stranded.
findings.actualState: When AD groups yield no role (or resolved role names are absent from the role table), the sync applies a fallback role SAML_DEFAULT_ROLE_NAME (default 'Branch Manager'); a two-tier bulletproof fallback ensures an authenticated RSA user is never left role-less unless the fallback role itself is missing from the DB (server/routes/auth.ts:357, :412-430; server/storage/sqlServerEmployee.ts:208-290).
findings.recommendedChange: Add a note that any authenticated user whose groups map to no ClientIQ role is granted the default fallback role (Branch Manager) so they are never stranded on 'Awaiting Role Assignment'.

findings.location: Owner and Data Classification lines on each group
findings.docSays: Each group lists an 'Owner' (e.g. Operations Administration Manager, Risk Manager, Compliance Manager, Application Services Manager) and 'Data Classification: Confidential'.
findings.actualState: Governance metadata (group owners, data classification) is not represented in the codebase and cannot be verified from source. Only the group-name → role mapping is code-verifiable (server/auth/adGroupRoleMap.ts).
findings.recommendedChange: Confirm the owner and data-classification values with the IAM/AD governance team; these fields are outside the code's scope and must be validated by the group owners of record.

docPurpose: Governance/process deployment plan for ClientIQ ("Banking Client 360") defining the Dev→Test→Pre-Prod→Prod promotion flow, environment gates, roles/responsibilities, branching model, per-environment deploy/rollback steps, and required documentation for software and data engineering.
summary: The document is a solid process/governance framework and much of it (cadence, roles, gates, rollback philosophy, required docs) still holds. However, its concrete technical claims are materially out of date: the branching model (develop / release/x.y / main) does not match the actual pipeline (develop / test / preprod / prod), and the "same commit/build promoted Test→Prod" key rule contradicts the ADO pipeline, which triggers a fresh build per branch and deploys Prod from the `prod` branch rather than a promoted Test artifact. Several current realities are undocumented: SQL Server is the only production DB engine (never named), Prod deploys to two servers, the deployed runtime actually runs `tsx watch` from TypeScript source under NODE_ENV=development, dependency install is gated on the literal "npm ci" commit message, and SAST=SonarQube (develop-only) / DAST=OWASP ZAP (post-Test, fails on any high) are not identified. No PostgreSQL-specific claims appear in the doc itself, but the migration tooling it implies (drizzle-kit) points at a PostgreSQL config, which is worth calling out. Staleness is moderate: the skeleton is reusable but the technical specifics need correction.

findings.location: Section 4. Source Control & Branching (branch table: develop / release/x.y / main)
findings.docSays: Branches are: `develop` (Active development), `release/x.y` (Test & Prod candidate), `main` (Production state).
findings.actualState: The ADO pipeline keys entirely off four branches — `develop`, `test`, `preprod`, `prod` — with stage conditions eq(Build.SourceBranch,'refs/heads/develop'|'test'|'preprod'|'prod') (azure-pipelines.yml:106,131,177,203,229) and trigger on develop/test/preprod (azure-pipelines.yml:1-4). There is no `release/x.y` branch and no `main`/`master` reference anywhere in azure-pipelines.yml or PipelineTemplates/. Per project ops, preprod/prod deploy from these ADO branches, NOT GitHub `main`.
findings.recommendedChange: Replace the branch table with the real model: develop→Dev, test→Test (+DAST), preprod→Pre-Prod, prod→Prod. Remove `release/x.y` and `main`. Add an explicit note that GitHub `main` is not a deploy source; deployments come from the ADO branches.

findings.location: Section 4. Source Control & Branching — Key Rule
findings.docSays: Key Rule: The same commit/build must go from Test to Prod.
findings.actualState: The pipeline does not promote a single Test artifact to Prod. Each branch push triggers its own Build stage and then a branch-gated deploy stage; Prod deploys are gated on `refs/heads/prod` (azure-pipelines.yml:203,229), i.e. a build produced from the `prod` branch, not the artifact that was validated in Test (which is built from the `test` branch, azure-pipelines.yml:131). The artifact is rebuilt per branch, so 'same commit/build Test→Prod' is only true if the identical commit is advanced through each branch — it is not enforced by the pipeline.
findings.recommendedChange: Either correct the statement to reflect that promotion is by advancing the same commit through develop→test→preprod→prod (with a rebuild at each stage), or, if a true build-once-promote-many model is desired, note that the current pipeline does not implement it and rebuilds per branch.

findings.location: Section 2. Environment Overview / throughout (database engine not named)
findings.docSays: References 'Separate infrastructure and databases per environment', 'schema changes', and 'schema migrations' generically without naming a database engine.
findings.actualState: SQL Server (MSSQL) is the only production database engine. The runtime connection manager is 'MS SQL Server only (on-prem deployment)' (server/dbConnection.ts:1-4); getPgDatabase() throws 'this deployment uses MS SQL only' (server/dbConnection.ts:74-79). Start scripts and the ADO deploy set DATABASE_DIALECT=sqlserver / DB_VENDOR=mssql with MSSQL_* connection vars (PipelineTemplates/start-script.yml:19-28).
findings.recommendedChange: State explicitly that the production database engine is Microsoft SQL Server, and that each environment has its own SQL Server database (MSSQL_SERVER/MSSQL_DATABASE per env), so the data-engineering steps are unambiguous.

findings.location: Sections 6/8 Data Engineering steps ('Apply migrations') and Section 11 Required Documentation ('Migration scripts')
findings.docSays: Data Engineers 'Apply Test/production database migrations (backward-compatible / non-destructive)' and maintain 'Migration scripts' as required documentation.
findings.actualState: There is no SQL Server migration mechanism wired into the pipeline; the only schema tooling is `db:push` = `drizzle-kit push` (package.json:11) which is driven by drizzle.config.ts hard-coded to dialect 'postgresql' and requiring DATABASE_URL (drizzle.config.ts:3-14) — i.e. it targets PostgreSQL, not the production SQL Server. The pipeline (azure-pipelines.yml) contains no DB-migration step at all; schema changes to SQL Server are applied out-of-band.
findings.recommendedChange: Clarify how SQL Server schema changes are actually applied (manual scripts / out-of-band process) and note that drizzle-kit push targets the non-production PostgreSQL config, so it is not the production migration path. If migration scripts are the standard, document where they live and how they run against MSSQL.

findings.location: Section 8. Production Deployment Steps (Software Engineering)
findings.docSays: Prod deploy = 'Confirm current production version; Deploy new version; Validate health checks / error rates; Monitor.' Implies a single production deploy target.
findings.actualState: Production is deployed to TWO servers via two separate stages, Deploy_Prod (server 1) and Deploy_Prod2 (server 2), both gated on refs/heads/prod (azure-pipelines.yml:203,229) using variable groups VG-Prod and VG-Prod2 respectively (azure-pipelines.yml:206,232).
findings.recommendedChange: Document that Prod is a two-node deployment (two stages / two servers) and that both must be deployed and validated. Note the separate variable groups per node.

findings.location: Section 3 Roles ('Assess SAST/DAST scan results') and Section 6 Approval Gate ('includes Bank Security')
findings.docSays: Software Engineers 'Assess SAST / DAST scan results and remediate high / critical findings' — without naming tools, when they run, or whether they gate the build.
findings.actualState: SAST = SonarQube, runs ONLY on the `develop` branch (SonarQubePrepare/Analyze/Publish conditioned on refs/heads/develop, azure-pipelines.yml:38,67,71). DAST = OWASP ZAP, runs as a stage after Deploy_Test (dependsOn Deploy_Test + succeeded(), azure-pipelines.yml:156-158) and FAILS the build on any high finding (exit 1 when highs > allowedHighs=0, PipelineTemplates/dast-scan.yml:8,183-202).
findings.recommendedChange: Name the tools and their placement: SonarQube SAST on develop, OWASP ZAP DAST after the Test deploy with a zero-high gate. State that DAST failure blocks promotion so the gate is concrete.

findings.location: Sections 5/6/8 deploy steps ('Deploy to Dev/Test', 'Restart services', 'Deploy new version')
findings.docSays: Deploy steps are described abstractly ('Deploy to Dev', 'Restart services', 'Deploy new version') with no mention of the target platform or runtime.
findings.actualState: The app is deployed to Windows Servers via PowerShell Remoting into C:\ClientIQ and runs as a Windows Service (copy artifact → Stop-Service → optional npm ci → Start-Service; PipelineTemplates/deploy-nodejs.yml:16-38). The deployed process is launched as `npx tsx watch --clear-screen=false server/index.ts` — i.e. it runs TypeScript source in watch mode, not the compiled dist/index.js (PipelineTemplates/start-script.yml:48). A single un-firewalled port 5000 serves both API and client (server/index.ts:94-104).
findings.recommendedChange: Add a short technical deployment note: Windows Service in C:\ClientIQ, deployed over PowerShell Remoting, run via tsx watch on port 5000. This makes 'Restart services' and 'Deploy new version' actionable.

findings.location: Section 9. Rollback Strategy — Application Rollback
findings.docSays: Application Rollback: 'Re-deploy previous known-good artifact (stable version); Disable features via configuration; Restart services.'
findings.actualState: The published build artifact excludes node_modules (CopyFiles excludes node_modules/, azure-pipelines.yml CopyFiles step) and the deployed server runs from TypeScript source via tsx watch, with dependency install (npm ci) on the target only occurring when the commit message contains the literal 'npm ci' (PipelineTemplates/deploy-nodejs.yml:25-32; azure-pipelines.yml:59). So 'redeploy previous artifact' is only clean if dependencies did not change; a dependency-affecting rollback also needs an 'npm ci' redeploy.
findings.recommendedChange: Note the rollback caveat: because node_modules is excluded from the artifact and refreshed only on an 'npm ci' commit, a rollback that changes dependencies must include the npm-ci path; otherwise the previous artifact may run against mismatched node_modules.

findings.location: Sections 5/6/8 (dependency install / build behavior) and Section 11 (deployment checklists)
findings.docSays: No mention of how dependencies are installed on build agent or target, or of any commit-message-driven behavior.
findings.actualState: Dependency install is gated on the literal string 'npm ci' appearing in the commit message — on the build agent (condition: contains(Build.SourceVersionMessage,'npm ci'), azure-pipelines.yml:59) and again on the target server (if $commitMessage -match 'npm ci', PipelineTemplates/deploy-nodejs.yml:25-32). npm packages are pulled from the private Nexus proxy registry farmers-merchants-bank.repo.sonatype.app (azure-pipelines.yml:47).
findings.recommendedChange: Document the 'npm ci' commit-message convention as a required deployment step whenever dependencies change, and note the private Nexus registry. This is an operational gotcha that will silently skip dependency updates if omitted.

findings.location: Section 2, item 3 PRE-PROD Environment — 'Entry into TEST' / 'Exit from TEST' sub-bullets
findings.docSays: Under '3. PRE-PROD Environment' the entry/exit sub-bullets are labeled 'Entry into TEST' and 'Exit from TEST'.
findings.actualState: These are copy-paste labels from the TEST section; in the Pre-Prod block they should read 'Entry into PRE-PROD' / 'Exit from PRE-PROD'. This is a documentation labeling error, not a code fact.
findings.recommendedChange: Rename the Pre-Prod entry/exit bullets to 'Entry into PRE-PROD' and 'Exit from PRE-PROD'.

findings.location: Section 6. Approval Gate — 'Ready for Pre-Prod'
findings.docSays: Ready for Pre-Prod: 'build version complete, smoke test notes complete, deployment notes complete, build version complete.' ('build version complete' listed twice.)
findings.actualState: Duplicated criterion ('build version complete' appears twice) — an editorial error in the checklist.
findings.recommendedChange: Remove the duplicate 'build version complete' entry and confirm the intended Pre-Prod readiness criteria.

findings.location: Section 7 heading 'Production Deployment' vs its checklist heading 'Pre-Production Checklist (Mandatory)'
findings.docSays: Section 7 'Production Deployment' contains a checklist titled 'Pre-Production Checklist (Mandatory)'.
findings.actualState: Mismatched heading: the checklist gates the Production deployment (Test approved, rollback confirmed, on-call, monitoring, backups, coordinate with App Services & DBAs) but is titled 'Pre-Production'. This is an internal-consistency issue, not a code fact.
findings.recommendedChange: Rename to 'Pre-Deployment Checklist (Mandatory)' for Production, or clarify it is the go/no-go checklist executed before the production deploy.

findings.location: Section 1 Recommended Delivery Rhythm; Section 3 Roles & Responsibilities; Section 7 CAB/Segregation of Duties
findings.docSays: Cadence (1-week sprint, weekly/biweekly Prod), rotating Release Lead, QA/Product approvals, 'CAB/change approval obtained if applicable', 'Coordinated deployment with App Services & DBAs (Segregation of Duties)', 'Bank Security' sign-off.
findings.actualState: These are governance/ownership/process assertions that cannot be verified from the repository — no code artifact defines cadence, role assignments, CAB, or segregation-of-duties. The pipeline does show an environment-approval structure (ADO deployment environments Dev/Test/PreProd/Prod, azure-pipelines.yml) but not who approves them.
findings.recommendedChange: Confirm with the release/change-management owner that cadence, rotating Release Lead, CAB applicability, DBA/App Services segregation of duties, and Bank Security sign-off are current. Mark these as human-owned governance, not derived from code.

findings.location: Section 2 Environment Overview table — Test 'masked data' / Pre-Prod 'production data'
findings.docSays: Test (QA/UAT) uses 'Prod-like, masked data'; Pre-Prod uses 'production data'; Dev uses 'masked-production data only'.
findings.actualState: Data-masking and which environment holds production data are operational/data-governance facts not expressible in the repo. The code only shows per-environment MSSQL connection targets (e.g., dev DB 'ClientIQdev' in Start-Dev.ps1), not masking policy.
findings.recommendedChange: Have data engineering / data governance confirm the masking posture per environment (especially that Dev/Test truly use masked data and Pre-Prod uses production data), as this is compliance-sensitive and unverifiable from code.

docPurpose: Explains the ClientIQ / BankClient360 hybrid RBAC + ABAC authorization model: roles, privilege levels, permission codes, what each role sees in the UI, protected API routes, ABAC (employee-customer protection), permission resolution, DB schema, frontend hooks, role testing, and key files.
summary: The doc is largely accurate on the core model (5 privilege levels, 9 roles, 11 permissions, two-tier resolution, protected admin/account routes) and matches the seed/schema well. Its main problems are (1) it presents the ABAC employee-customer restriction as a single coherent, always-enforced control, but the codebase has a real split: the frontend uses a level<2 threshold while the backend seed uses minPrivilegeOverride:3, and in SQL Server (production) mode the PG permissionService ABAC check is a no-op — the doc never surfaces this gap; (2) it omits documented enforcement gaps (Notes and deposit-summary/deposit-trend endpoints are auth-only, not permission-gated); (3) it presents role_change_request and role_audit_log as live tables when they have no implementing/writing code; and (4) it retains a Postgres reference in Key Files and omits the audit_event stream entirely. No trigram/dual-database claims are present, but the "Postgres + SQL Server" data-access note and the unqualified ABAC-enforcement narrative are the notable database/behavior accuracy issues.

findings.location: Employee Customer Protection (ABAC) — intro line + table
findings.docSays: "The check is maxPrivilegeLevel < 2 — meaning only level 0 and level 1 users are restricted." The table then shows Level 2 (Manager) = "Yes / Full access to employee customer data" and only Levels 0-1 restricted.
findings.actualState: Two different thresholds exist and disagree. The FRONTEND uses maxPrivilegeLevel < 2 (client/src/components/CustomerDashboard.tsx:490 `const isLevel1User = maxPrivilegeLevel < 2;`), so it restricts levels 0-1 as the doc states. But the BACKEND seeded ABAC rule for transaction.view uses minPrivilegeOverride: 3 (scripts/seed.ts:142, reason 'Employee customer records require Level 3+ access'), which would deny levels 0,1,AND 2. The doc's own ABAC example section quotes minPrivilegeOverride: 3 (line 272), contradicting its own '< 2' prose and its 'Level 2 = Yes' table.
findings.recommendedChange: Split the explanation into two enforcement points with their true thresholds: frontend tab-hiding uses level < 2 (restricts levels 0-1); the backend transaction.view ABAC rule is seeded with minPrivilegeOverride: 3 (would restrict levels 0-2). Fix the table so Level 2 is not unconditionally 'Yes', or explicitly note the frontend/backend threshold mismatch.

findings.location: What Each Role Sees — Employee Customer Protection: "enforced at both layers" / Backend bullet; and How Permissions Are Resolved step 5 (ABAC evaluation)
findings.docSays: "This is enforced at both layers... Backend: Transaction API endpoints build ABAC context by checking all account owners for isEmployee === true and deny access if privilege level is insufficient." and step 5 "ABAC evaluation — If the permission is attribute-based, the context is built and conditions are evaluated."
findings.actualState: In production (SQL Server) mode the PG-path ABAC evaluation is a no-op: server/services/permissionService.ts:32-36 returns { allowed: true } early when db is null (SQL Server mode). The employee-customer isEmployee/minPrivilegeOverride condition is only evaluated by the Drizzle/PG permissionService path; the SQL Server store's own checkPermission (server/storage/roleManagement/sqlServer.ts) implements branchLevel/regionLevel restrictions, not the customer.isEmployee restriction (facts rbac.md §5.4, §11.3). So the backend transaction-level restriction may not actually fire in production. The route DOES still build the context (routes.ts:2345-2371), but the deny decision short-circuits to allow.
findings.recommendedChange: Add a caveat that the transaction.view employee-customer ABAC deny is fully evaluated only on the PG abstraction path; in SQL Server production mode permissionService.checkPermission returns allowed:true and enforcement depends on the SQL Server permission.conditions data (branch/region model), which does not encode the isEmployee rule. Flag this as a known enforcement gap requiring operator/dev verification.

findings.location: What Each Role Sees / Protected API Routes (enforcement gaps not documented)
findings.docSays: The doc lists protected routes and states sections are hidden/denied without permission, implying feature access is permission-gated. It documents customer.view.deposits as gating the Deposits section and lists note-free protected routes.
findings.actualState: Two enforcement gaps are undocumented. (1) Notes endpoints are authentication-only, NOT permission-gated: GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/notes* in server/routes.ts (2524, 2541, 2558, 2579, 2671, 2698, 2729, 2745, plus 2605/2644) have no requirePermission (the only requirePermission calls in routes.ts are at lines 1234, 1320, 2346, 2400, 2946-3102). There is no notes.* permission anywhere (facts rbac.md §7.1). The Notes UI is rendered with no PermissionGuard (CustomerDashboard.tsx:863-869). (2) GET /api/customers/:id/deposit-summary (routes.ts:1271) and /deposit-trend (routes.ts:1293) have NO requirePermission, even though the sibling /deposit-recent-transactions (routes.ts:1319) requires transaction.view. So customer.view.deposits gates only the UI region, not these two server endpoints.
findings.recommendedChange: Add an 'Enforcement gaps' subsection: Notes are readable/writable by any authenticated employee regardless of role (no notes.* permission exists, no server guard, no PermissionGuard); and deposit-summary/deposit-trend endpoints are auth-only despite the customer.view.deposits UI gate. Clarify that client-side PermissionGuard is the only gate for these features.

findings.location: Database Schema — Audit & Compliance Tables (role_audit_log, role_change_request)
findings.docSays: Lists role_audit_log "Tracks all role assignment changes" and role_change_request "Workflow for role change approvals" as core audit/compliance tables, presented as active parts of the system.
findings.actualState: Both tables are defined in shared/schema.ts (role_audit_log schema.ts:744-762; role_change_request schema.ts:825-848) but have no implementing/writing code. A repo-wide grep for roleChangeRequest/role_change_request finds no references outside schema.ts — no routes/services create or approve requests (facts rbac.md §9.4). role_audit_log has no writer in server code; the app audits via audit_event + employee_role_history + permission_denial_log instead (facts rbac.md §9.5). Role changes happen via direct admin assign/remove endpoints and SAML/AD sync, not an approval workflow.
findings.recommendedChange: Annotate both tables as 'defined in schema but not yet implemented / no writer in current code'. Note that role changes today go through direct admin assign/remove endpoints and automated SAML/AD sync, and that actual audit persistence uses audit_event, employee_role_history, and permission_denial_log.

findings.location: Database Schema / How Permissions Are Resolved (audit_event stream not documented)
findings.docSays: The doc mentions AUTHZ_PERMISSION_GRANTED / AUTHZ_PERMISSION_DENIED audit events and permission_denial_log, but never documents the audit_event table or the unified audit-event stream that backs those events.
findings.actualState: There is a unified audit_event table (shared/schema.ts:854-887) and taxonomy (shared/auditEvents.ts) with categories (authentication, authorization, pii_access, financial_data, data_modification, admin_action, navigation, search, error), severities, and event types including authz.permission.granted/denied, authz.role.assigned/removed, authz.role.test.start/end. Emitted/persisted by server/services/auditService.ts and the permission middleware (facts rbac.md §13). This is the actual backing store for the grant/deny events the doc references.
findings.recommendedChange: Add audit_event to the schema table list and briefly document the unified audit-event stream (auditService, auditEvents taxonomy), since the doc already references its event type names but never names the table or stream.

findings.location: Roles table / SAML section (BRS role and AD-group→role code mapping not documented)
findings.docSays: Lists 9 roles including 'Assistant Manager' and 'Business Banker' (both priv 2) and describes SAML integration only via the saml_role_mapping table ("Auto-assigns roles based on SAML identity attributes").
findings.actualState: Production role provisioning is driven by a CODE-based AD-group→role-name map (server/auth/adGroupRoleMap.ts), not the saml_role_mapping table, on the live ACS login path (facts rbac.md §10.5, §3.3). That map references a 'BRS' (Business Relationship Specialist, priv 2) role that businessbanker and assistantmanager AD tokens both resolve to (adGroupRoleMap.ts:48-49) — but BRS is NOT in scripts/seed.ts and no in-repo migration creates it. The doc's role list (Assistant Manager, Business Banker) does not match what AD-driven users actually resolve to.
findings.recommendedChange: Document that production role assignment uses the code-based AD-group convention map (adGroupRoleMap.ts) as the live mechanism, distinct from the admin-managed saml_role_mapping table. Note the BRS role that AD groups map to and flag that it is not created by seed.ts (must exist in SQL Server out-of-band). Reconcile the roles list with the AD map.

findings.location: Key Files — server/storage/roleManagement/ description
findings.docSays: "server/storage/roleManagement/ — Data access layer (Postgres + SQL Server)".
findings.actualState: The directory does contain both postgres.ts and sqlServer.ts (verified: ls of server/storage/roleManagement/ shows index.ts, postgres.ts, sqlServer.ts). However SQL Server is the only production engine; the Postgres store is an unused abstraction. The production read/write path is server/storage/roleManagement/sqlServer.ts and server/storage/sqlServerEmployee.ts (facts rbac.md ground-rule note).
findings.recommendedChange: Reword to make clear SQL Server is the production data-access layer (sqlServer.ts), with postgres.ts present only as a non-production abstraction. Avoid implying a live dual-database deployment.

findings.location: How Permissions Are Resolved — step 6 / permission_denial_log
findings.docSays: "Permission denials are also logged to the permission_denial_log table for compliance." (implies a single straightforward insert).
findings.actualState: There are two separate denial-logging mechanisms and a schema/SQL column-name divergence. The audit_event stream logs every grant AND deny; permission_denial_log logs denials. In the SQL Server path the INSERT uses columns reason + denied_at (sqlServer.ts:238-269), while the schema/PG path uses denial_reason + created_at (schema.ts:771,774; permissionService.ts:189). The SQL Server DB must physically have reason/denied_at columns for the insert to succeed (facts rbac.md §9.3, §11.4).
findings.recommendedChange: Optionally note that denials are recorded both in the unified audit_event stream and permission_denial_log, and that the SQL Server insert uses reason/denied_at columns (vs the schema's denial_reason/created_at) — a known schema-vs-code divergence.

findings.location: Role Testing (Non-Production) — audience wording / production guard
findings.docSays: "lets developers simulate different roles... ROLE_TESTING_ENABLED (defaults to true, set to false to disable). Production guard: Always disabled in NODE_ENV=production."
findings.actualState: Accurate on the mechanics: enabled unless ROLE_TESTING_ENABLED==='false' (roleTestService.ts:14), and setOverride throws if NODE_ENV==='production' (roleTestService.ts:19-22). But env-vars facts note deploy scripts set NODE_ENV=development for ALL environments (PipelineTemplates/start-script.yml), so unless the Windows service env overrides it, the production guard may not actually engage in deployed 'production' environments. Overrides are in-memory only (Map, lost on restart).
findings.recommendedChange: Keep the mechanics but add a caveat that the NODE_ENV=production guard only fires if the runtime NODE_ENV is actually 'production'; deploy templates set NODE_ENV=development, so verify the service env in higher environments. Optionally note overrides are in-memory and non-persistent.
